Select only supported models and efforts from current tool documentation or observed enumeration. A missing role line keeps the portable inherit-parent default. A role line of inherit-parent or auto omits explicit model selection. Unsupported configured models or efforts require a disclosed supported fallback, or blocked if that exact choice is required. The source-host named defaults are not portable availability evidence. Unknown observed models leave diversity unverified.\\n\\nWithout an exposed and authorized independent-worker operation, apply the same full-mode and leaf reads sequentially only within authorized scope. Label reduced capability. Sequential roles are not independent workers, independent review, background execution or model diversity. If the playbook requires independence, leave that gate blocked rather than silently waiving it.\\n\\nA worker forbidden to spawn owns its assigned diff directly and returns it to the lead for review separation, as Feature step 4 requires. Before accepting any result, match assignment identity, exact input revision, full current head SHA, existing artifacts and observed method evidence. Reject stale results and missing artifacts under the assignment contract. Bookkeeping labels cannot satisfy these checks.\\n\\nYou own every subagent's work. Review the diff and write your own summary, don't pass through what it said. A second opinion is the same prompt against a different model. Treat agreement as supporting evidence only after checking independence, the observed models and the underlying artifacts.\\n\\n**Fresh subagents by default.** Give new work to a fresh subagent with consolidated scope, meaning the original brief, every later directive, and the prior agent's report and branch. Resume, message, or queue a follow-up on an existing subagent only when the new work strictly needs state that lives in that agent and is costly to move: its local checkout, its uncommitted changes, or a process it still runs, such as a dev server, a simulator, or a babysit watcher. A stop or hold order to a running agent is not reuse. A role such as a PR owner outlives its agent. Once that agent returns, a fresh agent takes the role's next round. Interrupt-chained resumes silently drop directives, so fire a fresh subagent with consolidated scope rather than trusting a \\\"done\\\" summary.\\n\\n## Throughput checkpoint\\n\\nFor nontrivial multi-step work, write these four todo items before fan-out, as required by Feature step 3. Keep an inapplicable dimension with n/a and a reason. Rewrite the checkpoint at phase boundaries and return it with the evidence.\\n\\n- Blocking first steps. Default to splitting the target using the separate-before-serializing-shared-state principle leaf. Serialize only for real invariants.\\n- Smallest safe decomposition. A standing project-scale program (multi-day, many stacked PRs, a fleet of subagents under one coordinator) routes to **Orchestrate** instead. figure-it-out designs one bespoke run, orchestrate runs the program.\\n\\n- **Investigation.** Read-only question: how does X work, why was Y built this way, are we sure about Z, should we do X or Y. `playbooks/investigation.md`.\\n- **Bug fix.** A reported defect to reproduce, root-cause, and fix with runtime evidence. `playbooks/bug-fix.md`.\\n- **Perf issue.** A measured slowness to trace and improve against a baseline. `playbooks/perf-issue.md`.\\n- **Hillclimb.** Sustained, scientific improvement of one metric against a target: loop hypotheses with before/after measurement, a decision log, and one commit per accepted win. Never infer authorization from a bot comment.\\n\\nUse this reference when the Babysit playbook (`../playbooks/babysit.md`) handles Bugbot or review-automation comments. The goal is not to ignore Bugbot by default. The goal is to stop treating every comment as a required code change.\\n\\n## Decision rubric\\n\\nClassify each Bugbot thread before acting:\\n\\n- `fix`: The comment identifies a plausible correctness, security, privacy, data loss, auth, billing, migration, idempotency, race, or shipped-behavior issue. Fix it in the lowest owning PR, then reply with the commit SHA and resolve the thread.\\n- `dismiss`: The comment matches a documented low-risk noisy pattern, and the current code/context proves the concern does not need a code change. Reply with a short reason and resolve the thread.\\n- `ask`: The comment is novel, high-severity, security/privacy/data-related, or ambiguous. Ask the user instead of guessing.\\n\\nWhen in doubt, ask. Skipping a noisy code-quality comment is cheap; skipping a real data or security bug is not.\\n\\n## Learned pattern format\\n\\nAdd future patterns in this shape:\\n\\n```markdown\\n### <short pattern name>\\n\\n- Confidence: candidate | recurring | strong\\n- Skip when: <conditions that must be true>\\n- Do not skip when: <risk boundaries>\\n- Example signal: <phrases or code context that identify the pattern>\\n- Source: <PR/comment URL or short historical note>\\n```\\n\\nUse `candidate` for one or two examples. Use `recurring` after multiple real dismissals. Use `strong` only when the pattern is narrow, repeatedly verified, and low-risk.\\n\\n## Recurring skip candidates\\n\\n### Intentional UI or design-system visual changes\\n\\n- Confidence: candidate\\n- Skip when: The PR description, screenshots, design review, or nearby code makes the visual change explicit, and the Bugbot comment is only restating that a shared visual default changed.\\n- Do not skip when: The comment points to accessibility, focus visibility, keyboard navigation, color contrast, or a component API contract that the PR did not intentionally change.\\n- Example signal: Comments about focus outlines, button sizes, spacing, or shared component visual defaults where the owner replies \\\"intentional\\\" or \\\"intended\\\".\\n\\n### Upstack or stack-local usage Bugbot cannot see\\n\\n- Confidence: candidate\\n- Skip when: Bugbot flags an export, component, helper, or file as unused, and the active forge's PR list and diffs, upper-stack diffs, or PR context show it is used by a later PR in the stack.\\n- Do not skip when: The current PR is not part of a stack, the symbol is public API, or the supposed upstack use cannot be verified.\\n- Example signal: \\\"Exported component is never used\\\" with a human reply like \\\"used upstack\\\".\\n\\n### Temporary duplication during parallel implementation\\n\\n- Confidence: candidate\\n- Skip when: The PR intentionally duplicates a small amount of code to keep a new path parallel to an old path that is being deleted, replaced, or proven out.\\n- Do not skip when: The duplicated code changes security, billing, data access, API behavior, or a long-lived shared abstraction would clearly reduce risk.\\n- Example signal: \\\"Significant duplication\\\" or \\\"duplicated validation logic\\\" where the owner explains the old path will be deleted or the duplicate logic is intentionally local.\\n\\n### Existing framework or component invariant covers the warning\\n\\n- Confidence: candidate\\n- Skip when: The concern is already guaranteed by a shared component, framework contract, type invariant, or single source of truth visible in the current diff or nearby code.\\n- Do not skip when: The invariant is assumed but not enforced, depends on timing, or crosses async/state boundaries where values can diverge.\\n- Example signal: Comments about missing max-height on an inner popover when the shared popover enforces viewport bounds, or nullable values where the local checked value and passed value share the same source.\\n\\n### Owner-declared follow-up or deferred cleanup\\n\\n- Confidence: candidate\\n- Skip when: The PR owner explicitly says the issue is a known follow-up, the behavior is not made worse by the current PR, and the comment is not about a high-risk area.\\n- Do not skip when: The agent is acting without owner input, the issue is medium/high severity product behavior, or deferring would merge a new regression.\\n- Example signal: \\\"I'll worry about that later\\\" or \\\"we'll delete this eventually\\\".\\n\\n### Self-withdrawn or explicit false-positive rule comments\\n\\n- Confidence: recurring\\n- Skip when: The comment body or a later Bugbot reply explicitly says the finding is withdrawn, compliant, or a false positive, and the agent can verify the relevant rule locally.\\n- Do not skip when: The only evidence is a human saying \\\"false positive\\\" on a high-risk issue without explanation.\\n- Example signal: A file-naming rule comment whose body says the file is already compliant.\\n\\n## Ask by default\\n\\nDo not auto-skip these categories, even if a previous PR dismissed something similar:\\n\\n- Security, privacy, auth, billing, data retention, training-data, and permission-boundary findings.\\n- High-severity findings.\\n- Migration, schema, idempotency, concurrency, and cross-system behavior findings.\\n- Comments where the suggested fix is small and clearly reduces risk without changing product intent.\\n\\nHistorical data showed humans sometimes dismiss security/data-flow comments. Treat those as owner judgment calls, not team-wide skip rules.\\n\\n## Candidate learnings from recent babysits\\n\\nAppend new candidate learnings here during or after babysitting when they look team-useful but not yet mature. Prefer promoting recurring candidates into the section above once several PRs confirm the pattern.\\n\\n### Manual reimplementations of native browser behavior\\n\\n- Confidence: candidate\\n- Skip when: Practically never. When a diff replaces native browser behavior with a manual equivalent (native sticky → JS-positioned clones, native scroll targeting → forwarded wheel/touch events, paint-order occlusion → masks/clip-path), Bugbot's logic-bug findings against that code have been consistently legitimate.\\n- Do not skip when: The finding concerns event-forwarding gaps (wheel deltaMode, touch pans, scroll-chaining at edges, tap slop), mask/clip hit-testing divergence, or observer-vs-React state timing races in such code. Default to fix.\\n- Example signal: \\\"masks do not affect hit-testing\\\", \\\"overlay blocks wheel scroll\\\", \\\"ignores deltaMode\\\", \\\"runs in the IntersectionObserver callback before React applies state\\\".\\n- Source: one sticky-occlusion PR: six Bugbot passes, roughly eighteen findings, every one fixed rather than dismissed.\\n\\n### Contract-test drift claims are cheaply verifiable — run the test first\\n\\n- Confidence: candidate\\n- Skip when: Never skip the verification itself; it costs one command. When a PR\\n  ships a contract test that pins protocol or documentation prose (regexes over\\n  a SKILL.md, snapshot of doc wording), and Bugbot claims \\\"the test no longer\\n  matches the doc\\\" (or vice versa), run that test on the PR tip before\\n  classifying. A red run confirms the claim empirically; a green run is a\\n  concrete disproof for the dismissal reply.\\n- Do not skip when: n/a — this is a verification shortcut, not a dismissal\\n  pattern. Note that repeat-pass lean-dismiss heuristics would misfire here:\\n  prose-pinning tests drift precisely BECAUSE earlier fix rounds edit the prose.\\n- Example signal: \\\"Contract test omits the pre-fix wait\\\" on a PR whose earlier\\n  fix commits reworded the pinned passage; the test run on the tip failed on\\n  exactly the cited assertion.\\n- Source: one prose-pinning PR with eight Bugbot passes; the claim was real on\\n  pass 7 despite every earlier pass being fixed-and-resolved.\\n\\n### Stale security-review finding already fixed later in the same PR\\n\\n- Confidence: candidate\\n- Skip when: An agentic security review (or similar) claims a missing authz/validation call, and the current PR tip clearly includes that exact gate (with tests), typically added in a later hardening commit after the review ran.\\n- Do not skip when: The cited helper is a no-op for the principal under discussion, the check runs after the side effect it guards, or coverage for the claimed principal is missing.\\n- Example signal: A HIGH \\\"missing authorization check\\\" finding while the exact guard is already called before the side effect on the tip.\\n- Source: one webhook-endpoint PR whose hardening commit postdated the review run.\\n\\n### Widening a deliberately narrow error condition would mask the real error\\n\\n- Confidence: candidate\\n- Skip when: The finding asks to broaden a narrow error condition (a specific\\n  `errno`, error code, or status class) into a catch-all, and that narrowness\\n  encodes a real distinction. The canonical shape is a dependency fallback\\n  gated on `ENOENT`: \\\"binary is not installed\\\" is a different situation from\\n  \\\"the command ran and failed\\\". Retrying on any non-zero exit would re-run a\\n  legitimate failure (not found, expired auth, network) against the fallback\\n  and then report the fallback's error, hiding the true one.\\n- Do not skip when: The narrow condition misses a case in the SAME category\\n  (another \\\"binary unusable\\\" errno such as `EACCES`, another transport-level\\n  failure), the unhandled path loses data or leaves partial state, or the retry\\n  is idempotent AND the original error is still surfaced.\\n- Example signal: \\\"only retries when X fails with ENOENT … never tries the\\n  fallback even when a working Y exists\\\", pointing at code whose fallback\\n  exists for a missing dependency rather than a failed operation.\\n- Source: one CLI-rename PR whose fallback existed for a missing binary rather\\n  than a failed command.\\n\\nSOURCE /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/babysit.md\\n### Babysit\\n\\nApply the [assignment and action contract](../../../references/orchestration-contract.md). If ownership cannot be verified, do not start a competing babysitter.\\n\\n#### GitHub helper contract\\n\\nThe reviewed [watcher](../scripts/watch-pr/watch-pr) is GitHub-specific and read-only. Do not leave it running until merges happen. That is Shipping's job. If another actor merges the frontier and the watcher reports `ADVANCE`, continue with the new frontier. `COMPLETE` is terminal if another actor finishes the queue.\\n\\n   Watcher re-arms never authorize merging or arming merge-when-ready. Do not run `origin pr merge` or `gh pr merge` unless the user explicitly asked to merge, land, ship, or merge when ready. Route that request to `playbooks/shipping.md`. A stacked PR whose parent has no required checks may merge immediately into that parent when merge-when-ready is armed. This collapses review granularity. A lost-ref race can also mark it merged without updating the parent ref.\\n\\n   Answer a user question mid-loop and continue. An explicit stop, exhausted declared budget, denied operation or unavailable capability ends this invocation before the active forge's stop condition. Report the last observed state and unknowns; never silently reset the budget on rearm. On GitHub, that is `READY` in single or stack mode, or a `WAITING`/`merge-queue` report or `COMPLETE` in queued mode. On Origin, that is the merge-ready state defined above. For a GitHub queued stack, capture the PR list bottom-to-top once and pass the same frozen list to every rearm. Revise the list only for the sanctioned follow-up PR from step 4. Append it at the end, drop the merged owner, and rearm with the corrected snapshot.\\n7. **Classify CI before any retrigger.** Flake or infrastructure earns one fresh build, never a job retry. One retry only. An identical second failure means it was never flake, so reclassify and read the child logs instead of retrying blind. A failure in code the diff never touches means a stale base, so check with `git merge-base --is-ancestor` before assuming flake. Report a stale base as needing a rebase instead of burning retries. Only a failure in the diff's own code gets a commit.\\n8. **Bugbot is triaged skeptically, always.** Verify each claim against the code per `../references/bugbot-triage.md`. Fix real findings with a red-first proof in the lowest PR that owns the code, never at the tip unless the owning PR has merged. In that case, use step 4's sanctioned follow-up PR. Per step 2, upstack fixes wait for step 5's next frontier-driven push wave. Push that wave before replying so the reply cites the commit. On Origin, reply with `origin pr thread reply <thread-id> <pr> --body-file <reply-file>`. On GitHub, call `gh api --method POST \\\"repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<pr>/comments/<comment-id>/replies\\\" --input <payload.json>` and put the reply body in the JSON file as data. Never interpolate comment text or a reply into a shell command. Dismiss noise with the concrete disproof on the thread. On GitHub, use the watcher's Bugbot pass count. On Origin, derive the pass count from `origin pr thread list` and the review history. From the third pass on, lean toward dismissing documented patterns, still escalating anything touching security, auth, billing, data, or migrations rather than dismissing it yourself. Never churn code to quiet a bot.\\n9. **Stop at the human's line.** Owner approval is a wait, not a blocker to fix. Babysitting never authorizes merging. Only an explicit request to merge, land, ship, or merge when ready does. Route that request to Shipping. Surface the escalation and keep working the rest. After GitHub reports `READY`, a queued `WAITING`/`merge-queue` stop, or `COMPLETE`, or after Origin reports the frontier merge-ready, sweep the run's triage decisions once. Offer any team-useful dismissal pattern as a candidate entry in the shared rubric (`../references/bugbot-triage.md`) and its own PR. Never keep it only in private memory.\\n\\n`drive` ends at merge-ready. Landing the stack is `playbooks/shipping.md`.\\n\\n**Reply:** the mode, the frontier and its active-forge state, the watcher's four-column table on GitHub, what you fixed versus dismissed with reasons, what is still pending, and what needs the human.\\n\\nReview-thread collection must finish all pages before readiness. Missing/repeated cursors, changed totals, duplicate threads and failed pages leave status unavailable. Stack auto-discovery is supported only below its 300-open-PR enumeration cap; reaching the cap blocks completeness. Supply a separately verified explicit stack when auto-discovery is blocked. An UNKNOWN forge merge state or mergeable value is status unavailable, retried only within the existing poll/error/time budget. Status-only JSON and the Merge cell preserve unknown; neither is readiness.\\n\\nThe inherited non-UNKNOWN policy still distinguishes explicit conflicts and every BLOCKED forge state from other states. Known MERGEABLE with CLEAN, BEHIND, DRAFT, HAS_HOOKS or UNSTABLE can pass only after independently observed clean checks, no unresolved threads and satisfied actual draft/review gates. BLOCKED always refuses readiness, including a successful head rollup: it reports forge-blocked without inventing individual failed checks. These are the existing helper policy states; the forge state string alone never establishes readiness. That deliberate rule does not make UNKNOWN an allowed state or authorize a merge.\\n\\nSOURCE /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/shipping.md\\n### Shipping\\n\\n**You own what lands. Verify each PR independently, land only the verified run from the root, then keep your hands off the queue.**\\n\\nThis is the half after [babysit](babysit.md). It owns requests to land or ship. Apply [workflow ownership](../../../references/workflow-ownership.md), [session capabilities](../../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../../references/model-roles.md) and the [assignment and action contract](../../../references/orchestration-contract.md).\\n\\nRecord the active forge, repository, exact trunk tip, frozen bottom-to-top PR list and each verifier assignment before action. Check explicit user authorization for merge or merge-when-ready. Posting verdicts, publishing branches and retargeting each require their own authorized scope and available binding. Verification alone authorizes none of them. Prepare local artifacts when writes are denied. After interruption, inspect the prior action identity and destination before replay; an unknown outcome blocks replay.\\n\\nUse the caller's watch budget or at most 10 snapshot attempts and 600 seconds for this invocation. Carry the remaining budget across re-arms and merges. Stop on user stop, exhausted budget, denied access or unavailable operation, preserving the last observed frontier and unknowns. Use an exposed authorized loop or wake binding when available. Without one, a bounded foreground watch is reduced capability and registers no background continuation. A helper deadline is checked between reads and sleeps; it is not a hard wall-clock bound. Use an observed stop or execution-deadline binding for that guarantee, or disclose the limitation.\\n\\n1. **Resolve the forge, then verify every PR independently.** GitHub CLI (`gh`) is the default. If `command -v origin` succeeds and Origin can resolve the repository, use `origin pr ...` for PR view, watch, edit, and merge operations. Otherwise stay on `gh` and record the fallback. Never require Graphite (`gt`). One subagent per PR, not batched, each an independently spawned worker through an observed host binding, each exercising the real surface with the matching exposed and authorized control skill against exact parent versus head revisions. The upstream examples `control-ui` and `control-cli` are external skills, not bundled bindings. Missing control capability leaves real-surface verification blocked. Use inherited model roles unless current supported selection and actual results are observed. Each returns `PASS`, `PASS+NOTES` or `FAIL`, with verifier identity, exact revisions and method artifacts, and posts that verdict on its own PR when comment authorization exists. Otherwise retain the verdict locally and report that posting is blocked. A missing worker permits local sequential recommendations as reduced capability, never an independent verdict or a landable run. Safe means a verdict from an agent that did not write the code. CI green is not a verdict, and an approving bot review is not a verdict.\\n2. **Land only the contiguous verified run rooted at the bottom.** Walk up from the lowest unmerged PR and stop at the first one without a passing verdict, where both `PASS` and `PASS+NOTES` pass. A verified PR sitting above an unverified one is not landable. Report the ceiling as a PR number and say what breaks the chain.\\n3. **Re-check that each verdict still describes the patch.** Record the verdict head SHA, base SHA, and stable `git patch-id` of that PR's base-to-head diff. A rebase or base retarget rewrites SHAs and can silently invalidate a verdict without touching a check. Before landing a PR, read and record its current exact head SHA and base SHA, resolve the base-to-head diff at those revisions, and compare the recorded patch-id with its current base-to-head patch-id. Re-read the head and base immediately before the authorized merge or arm action. If either moved since the freshness check, stop and repeat that check. When the two patches differ only in tests, docs, or lint config, build what each lane ran. Build it twice at the verdict SHA and once at the current head. A difference is noise if the two builds at the verdict SHA also show it, or if it is an embedded commit SHA. Judge each difference, not each file, and report each kind of noise with its files. If only noise differs, that lane's result stays valid, and checks and a review of the change run fresh. Do not reuse a lane result from a dev server or from anything else with no build output. Rerun that lane. Re-verify anything else when the patch changed. When it did not, keep the code verdict but re-run mergeability and CI at the current head. Never use matching commit messages or a green check from an older SHA as a substitute.\\n4. **Prepare only the bottom PR.** Fetch current trunk. Rebase the lowest verified branch onto the exact trunk tip when needed, push it, and retarget only that PR to trunk through an exposed built-in PR tool when present, as required by [opening a PR](opening-a-pr.md). Without that tool use `origin pr edit <pr> --base <trunk>` or `gh pr edit <pr> --base <trunk>`. Re-run step 3 after the push. Do not retarget, arm, or merge descendants yet.\\n5. **Land one PR at a time.** If the bottom PR is mergeable now, squash it with `origin pr merge <pr> --squash` or `gh pr merge <pr> --squash`. If requirements are still running and the user asked for merge-when-ready, arm only that PR with `origin pr merge <pr> --squash --auto` or `gh pr merge <pr> --squash --auto`. Origin's `--auto` is Origin merge-when-ready. GitHub's `--auto` is GitHub auto-merge. Wait for that PR to merge before preparing the next one.\\n6. **Do not read GitHub `autoMergeRequest` as stack readiness.** At most it says GitHub auto-merge was requested for one GitHub PR. It does not prove Origin merge-when-ready is armed, that a descendant is queued, that a patch verdict is current, or that the contiguous stack is safe. Confirm the active forge's state for the current bottom PR, and say that the state is unknown if the active forge cannot report it.\\n7. **Recompute after every merge.** Fetch trunk, confirm the merged SHA is present, drop the merged PR from the frozen bottom-to-top list, and inspect the new bottom PR's base, head, checks, and patch-id. A host may retarget a child automatically, but do not assume it did. Repeat steps 3 through 6 for that one PR. Independent work stays outside this chain and ships on its own.\\n8. **Watch the current frontier until it merges or fails. Do not mutate the queue around it.** With Origin, use `origin pr view <pr> --checks --comments` and `origin pr checks <pr> --watch`, then re-read the PR until it reports merged or blocked. With GitHub, use the read-only [watcher](../scripts/watch-pr/watch-pr) from the package root as `bun --no-install skills/poteto-mode/scripts/watch-pr/watch-pr --owner <owner> --repo <repo> --queued-stack --stack-prs <bottom> --head <bottom=full-40-character-head> --max-polls <remaining-count> --timeout <remaining-seconds>` only as an event wake and poll `gh pr view <pr> --json state,mergedAt,mergeStateStatus,statusCheckRollup,autoMergeRequest` after each wake, ignoring `READY` until `mergedAt` is non-null or `state` is `MERGED`. Only then run step 7. Hard-fail only when `state` is `CLOSED` with no `mergedAt`, a required check concludes `FAILURE` or `CANCELLED` and blocks merge after auto-merge is no longer pending, or `mergeStateStatus` is `UNSTABLE` or `DIRTY` with no auto-merge pending. `BLOCKED` while checks are pending or auto-merge is armed is not failure. Do not use Babysit's queued `WAITING`/`merge-queue` stop condition here. Hold the watch through the observed authorized loop or wake binding within the declared budget. Do not add a second sleep loop. The watcher emits NDJSON schemaVersion 1 events. Inspect kind, terminal and reason, never exit 0 alone. Queued mode emits non-terminal `WAITING` with `reason.kind` equal to `merge-queue`, not `READY`. Terminal helper blockers or budget exhaustion require inspection of the active forge, not an invented merged or hard-failed state. The [bootstrap](../scripts/bootstrap.ts) checks pinned dependencies and fails setup-required; never install or bypass it. [Helper setup](../../../docs/testing/helper-setup.md) is separately authorized. For Origin, use a finite bound and an observed stop binding for check watching, or bounded view snapshots when an unbounded watch cannot be stopped. Report each merge and the new ceiling. If the queue stalls, diagnose before mutating.\\n9. **Stop at the ceiling.** When the verified run is merged, report what landed, what the next unverified PR is, and what verifying it would take. Extending the run is a new pass through step 1.\\n\\n**Reply:** the verified run and its ceiling, each PR's verdict and who produced it, what you armed and how you confirmed it, what landed, and what the next gap needs.\\n\\nSOURCE /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/swarm/SKILL.md\\n---\\nname: swarm\\ndescription: \\\"Fan out N parallel workers, drain them, and return one report. Use for /swarm, 'swarm this', or parallel coverage, races, gauntlets, and exploration.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Swarm\\n\\nFan out N independent parallel workers. They may cover separate slices, race the same brief, or mix both. The parent waits, aggregates, and returns one report. Invocation metadata expresses upstream intent; do not assume the host enforces it.\\n\\nUse [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md), and the [assignment contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Discover exposed operations and confirm authorization before dispatch. Upstream cloud/background execution and cloud branch selection require corresponding observed host bindings. Do not create remote branches or install capabilities as an incidental step.\\n\\n## Start\\n\\nOpen a task list with one entry per phase before launching anything. Use an in-chat list if no task-list tool is exposed.\\n\\n1. Frame\\n2. Fan out\\n3. Aggregate\\n4. Report\\n\\n## Phase A: Frame\\n\\n1. State the done predicate and the artifact or report the swarm must return.\\n2. Choose the shape. Partition into slices, race N workers on identical briefs, or mix both. For a race or mixed shape, declare `first pass`, `rank all`, or `best-of` before spawning.\\n3. Set N from the user or derive it from the shape. N is total workers, not the host concurrency limit.\\n4. Select the swarm worker model through current exposed model capabilities and the user's selection. The canonical configured/default model policy is host-specific; do not assume its model slug is supported here. For `auto` or `inherit-parent`, omit explicit model selection where the operation supports inheritance. Disclose any rejection and replacement. Use a supported same-family alternative when available and authorized, otherwise inherited selection; block an arm that requires an unavailable exact model. For a model race, name each arm's requested model up front and record actual models only when observed. Unknown actual models leave diversity unverified.\\n5. Give each worker its own writable output when it writes. When workers verify or measure commits, each brief names the exact full SHAs. A measurement brief also names the method, including sample count, what one sample is, and order. The worker records both in its result. Create immutable assignments and append-only attempt events under the assignment contract. Distinct output ownership applies even when race briefs are identical.\\n\\n## Phase B: Fan out\\n\\nDispatch all N assignments as one fan-out batch through exposed independent-worker operations, within actual concurrency limits. Prefer cloud/background execution when supported and authorized. Use local execution only when the worker needs something on the user's computer. If the host cannot provide the requested environment, disclose the limit before an authorized alternative. A non-default pushed branch requires an exposed base-branch binding and exact revision verification; never infer checkout from a branch label.\\n\\nEvery brief stands alone. Include the goal, scope, exact slice or race arm, how to verify, and what to report. Reports use `PASS`, `ISSUES`, or `BLOCKED` with evidence and links to existing artifacts. A worker that can prove a defect reports `ISSUES` and lists every issue it can prove, not only the first. Keep these report labels separate from assignment terminal states.\\n\\nIf a worker drops out, proceed with N-1 and note it. Record interrupted execution and retain the affected slice as a coverage gap unless another valid assignment covers it.\\n\\nUnavailable or denied independent execution blocks full swarm behavior. Authorized sequential work is reduced capability. Preserve slice briefs and evidence checks, but do not claim parallel workers, independent results, background execution or race parity.\\n\\n## Phase C: Aggregate\\n\\nWait for terminal results and inspect each result and its artifacts. Drop a result that does not record the SHAs and method its brief names, and respawn that worker once after inspecting the prior attempt and confirming permissions. Keep the same assignment identity, revision, scope and output ownership, and record the retry event. After a second miss, record a gap. A gap does not count as a pass. Missing artifacts and stale revisions also prevent acceptance; they do not become success through retry policy.\\n\\nFor coverage, every required slice needs a valid result. For a race, apply the selection rule declared up front. Use first pass, rank all, or best-of. Do not paste raw worker dumps. Selecting a winner does not hide gaps in required coverage.\\n\\nKeep a compact result table, one-line evidenced issues, and explicit gaps or dropouts. Cancel workers only through authorized exposed stop bindings. Inspect terminal state and quarantine partial artifacts from integration. If stopping cannot be observed, say termination is unverified. Cancellation never makes partial output a pass. Preserve durable assignment records with readback when available; missing persistence leaves recovery limits visible.\\n\\n## Phase D: Report\\n\\nReturn one consolidated in-chat report with the table, issue one-liners, gaps or dropouts, and the race rule when used. Include capability reductions, blocked assignments, fallback model selections, cancellation limits and unverified coverage. A source review or structural check never proves host behavior.\\n\\nSOURCE /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/no-comments/SKILL.md\\n---\\nname: no-comments\\ndescription: \\\"Spawn Comment Sicko, fix accepted findings, and offer encodings for claimed constraints.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# No comments\\n\\nSpawn Comment Sicko. Act on accepted findings.\\n\\nDefer to Comment Sicko's fresh perspective.\\n\\n## Scope\\n\\nUse the caller's files or diff. Otherwise use the current diff against the base branch, default `main`, including the working tree.\\n\\n## Steps\\n\\n1. Discover the independent-worker tools exposed in this session through [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md). Spawn an independent worker with the [Comment Sicko role](../../references/agent-prompts/comment-sicko.md) under the [orchestration contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md), following [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md) and [workflow ownership](../../references/workflow-ownership.md). Pass the scope. Do not restate its rules.\\n2. Inspect its report and diff. Reject application-code edits, scope escapes, exception-protected deletions, misstated `MUST KILL` reasons, and flags that treat kept intentional code as guilty. Reshape flags on our-code surprises stay actionable. Do not restore those comments. A keep survives only with proof it is about something we cannot change. Audit missed scoped lint and TypeScript suppressions. Correctness or safety suppressions stay actionable `MUST KILL`s. Restore deletions only with exact exceptions and scoped proof. Before accepting thin `IMPORTANT` or `do not remove` kills or keeps, run `/how` or `/why` using [how](../how/SKILL.md) or [why](../why/SKILL.md) on their symbol. If a kill is ambiguous, do not restore. If a keep is refuted or still ambiguous, delete it. Revert and rerun one rejected report with the failure named. Reject a second, report it open, and fail `/no-comments`.\\n3. Fix trivial accepted flags directly by deleting a dead path, dropping a parameter, or using the real API. If any fix needs a shape, run `/architect` using [architect](../architect/SKILL.md) once for the accepted set and surrounding code. Stop at the sketch. Architect shapes. Step 4 implements.\\n4. Implement the smallest root-cause fix in scope. Remove every named workaround. If the root cause is out of scope, land the smallest in-scope fix and report the rest open. The [principle-fix-root-causes](../principle-fix-root-causes/SKILL.md) and [principle-redesign-from-first-principles](../principle-redesign-from-first-principles/SKILL.md) skills guide intent only. Neither authorizes widening the fence nor fixing instances outside it. Never bolt on symptom guards.\\n5. Constraint comments say `do not remove`, `do not change wording`, or `talk to X before changing`. Leave keeps about things we cannot change. Offer the cheapest in-scope type, runtime, test, or CI lint. Wait for interactive approval. Unattended and eval require caller pre-approval. If approved, encode then delete. Otherwise delete, report the constraint open, and sketch out-of-scope work.\\n6. Report the deletion count, restored comments, reruns, architect sketch, fixes, encoding offers, encodings, unenforced constraints, and other open work.\\n\\n## Capability and permission limits\\n\\nThe Comment Sicko role edits only scoped comments when writes are authorized and available. Its final response is a report; that format does not prohibit its comment edits. This coordinator reviews those edits and implements accepted application-code fixes in steps 3 and 4, within caller authorization and scope. Verify edits before reporting deletion counts. Legal and license headers, justified public API contracts, and the role's other proven exceptions survive.\\n\\nIf independent workers are unavailable, use an authorized sequential review as reduced capability, retaining the same scope, investigations and review rules. Authorized scoped comment deletion and accepted fixes can still proceed. Do not claim a fresh independent perspective or a worker result.\\n\\nIf writes are denied, unavailable or unauthorized, use an authorized reduced read-only review. Report proposed deletions and fixes, actual deletion count zero, and unimplemented encodings and constraints. If actual edits are required and no reduction is authorized, report blocked. Missing scope, base branch, role or required investigative skill is a stated limit. Do not invent inspection or verdicts; report affected findings as skips and leave unresolved claims open.\\n\\nStep 5 does not grant write permission. Without encoding approval, delete the unprotected comment only when scoped comment writes are authorized and available; otherwise report its proposed deletion and the constraint open. Unattended or eval execution never supplies approval by itself.\\n\\nSOURCE /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/principle-prove-it-works/SKILL.md\\n---\\nname: principle-prove-it-works\\ndescription: \\\"Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.'\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Prove It Works\\n\\nVerify every task output by checking the real thing directly. Do not infer from proxies, self-reports, or \\\"it compiles.\\\"\\n\\n**Why:** Unverified work has unknown correctness. Indirect verification (file mtimes, output freshness, agent self-reports, cached screenshots) feels cheaper than direct observation. Acting on a wrong inference costs far more than checking the source.\\n\\nCheck the real thing, not a proxy:\\n- Check process liveness directly, not indirectly through derived state\\n- Read the actual value, not a cached or derived representation\\n- When verification fails, suspect the observation method before suspecting the system\\n\\n## Script the check when you can\\n\\nThe strongest proof is a deterministic script that re-runs the same comparison, not a one-time eyeball. Write the script, run it, and keep its output as an artifact a reviewer can re-run instead of trusting your word.\\n\\nKeep the artifact visible for the human. Commit it only for large or complex work where the trail has to be auditable later, like a big port or migration (the **show-me-your-work** skill).\\n\\n## Session capabilities and permissions\\n\\nUse the exposed tools and observed operations described in [host capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md). Run checks and retain artifacts only within the user's authorized scope and host permissions. If direct inspection or execution is unavailable or denied, state which outputs remain unverified and withhold completion for those outputs. A proposed script is not evidence that it ran.\\n\\nSOURCE /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/show-me-your-work/SKILL.md\\n---\\nname: show-me-your-work\\ndescription: \\\"Keep a reviewable decision trail for long-running or unattended work: a TSV log with one row per decision (what, why, evidence, result). Local by default; commit it when a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result. Use for /show-me-your-work, autonomous or multi-phase runs, or work a human reviews after stepping away.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Show me your work\\n\\nKeep one canonical log.\\n\\n## The format\\n\\nA single TSV file, one row per decision. Cells stay single-line. Evidence is a pointer, not prose.\\n\\nCopy [references/decision-log-template.tsv](references/decision-log-template.tsv) (the header row) to start a clean log. Columns:\\n\\n- **ts.** ISO8601 timestamp.\\n- **phase.** The phase or workstream.\\n- **decision.** What was chosen or done, one line.\\n- **why.** The reason in plain words. If a principle drove it, say it plainly, not as a jargon tag.\\n- **evidence.** A link or path that proves it: commit SHA, PR number, `file:line`, or an artifact, trace, or screenshot path. Never a paragraph.\\n- **result.** The outcome or predicate state: `tests green`, `reverted`, `pixel-diff 0`, `INCONCLUSIVE`, `open`.\\n\\nAn example, plain-spoken so a reviewer reads it at a glance.\\n\\n```\\nts\\tphase\\tdecision\\twhy\\tevidence\\tresult\\n2026-05-24T09:02:00Z\\tframe\\tcounted the work first, about 100 components and roughly 75 hours\\twanted to know the size before starting a long run\\tcommit 3a9f1c2\\tfound 5 things to sort out before starting\\n2026-05-24T09:40:00Z\\tharness\\ttook screenshots of the old version before changing anything\\tso we can compare old against new and catch any visual change\\tscripts/snapshot.sh, baseline/\\tsaved 120 reference screenshots\\n2026-05-24T11:15:00Z\\twidget\\tmoved the widget styles over without changing how it looks\\tkeep the change small and the result identical\\tcommit 7c21e0a, pixel-diff 0\\tlooks identical, tests pass\\n2026-05-24T12:30:00Z\\twidget\\tthrew out a helper's work because its screenshots were blank\\tchecked the real files instead of trusting its summary\\tworktree reset\\treverted, tightened the instructions for next time\\n```\\n\\n## Logging a row\\n\\nWrite each entry the way you'd tell a teammate what you did. Plain words, concrete actions, no AI speak or abstract jargon (the **unslop** skill applies to log text too).\\n\\nUse the helper [scripts/log.sh](scripts/log.sh) with `<logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>` through an authorized execution binding. Pass an explicit nonempty local output path that this task owns. The helper rejects tabs, newlines and carriage returns in any argument before creating directories or writing bytes. It stamps `ts`, writes the header on first use, preserves previous rows, and prefixes any cell starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, or `@` with a single quote. Use this helper for generated or user-supplied cells so validation and formula protection apply consistently. Host execution still requires an authorized binding.\\n\\nLog decision points and checkpoints, not every action: a fork chosen, a unit completed with its verification result, a pivot or revert with its trigger, a blocker surfaced, a gate fixed. For loop runs, one row per iteration. Skip the trivial and self-evident.\\n\\nA run is one agent conversation, including its later turns and any summary of it. A pickup, a replacement agent, or a new chat starts a new run. When a run adds to a log that already has rows, its first row has phase `start`, and so does its first row after another run's `start` row. So a run that comes back to a log in a later turn first reads the log's last rows to see whether another run wrote since. A `start` row names the `ts` range of the rows before it that this run did not write, and its evidence names this run, such as its agent id. Use phase `start` for nothing else.\\n\\n## Where it lives\\n\\nBy default the log is a working artifact, not committed. Keep it at `decisions.tsv` in the work dir, or `.audit/<task-slug>.tsv` when several efforts run at once, and leave it out of git.\\n\\nCommit it only when the work is ambitious enough that a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result.\\n\\n## Rules\\n\\n- Append-only. A wrong call gets a new row that supersedes it. Never edit or delete history.\\n- Prefer evidence produced by committed scripts over hand-made one-offs (the **encode-lessons-in-structure** principle skill).\\n\\n## Audit the log against the transcript\\n\\nAt the end of the run, before handing back, check the log told the truth. Discover this run's transcript through the current session's history binding, or an explicitly identified transcript in the active workspace. The source used `agent-transcripts/`; do not assume the host provides that directory. Never search unrelated private chats or global transcript directories. Freeze source coordinates\\n\\nBefore making a work list or delegating:\\n\\n1. Require the trigger channel to equal the configured source channel.\\n2. Send only with `channel=SOURCE_CHANNEL_ID` and `thread_ts=SOURCE_THREAD_TS`.\\n4. Read the thread again and verify the new message is a reply.\\n\\nIf any check fails, post nothing. Never retry at the root or in a fallback channel.\\n\\n## 2. Wait for the triage contract\\n\\nWatch the source thread for the configured verdict budget. Stay silent while waiting.\\n\\nAccept a verdict only when:\\n\\n- Its author matches `slack.triage_identity_user_id`.\\n- It is a reply under `SOURCE_THREAD_TS`.\\n- It contains exactly one configured marker.\\n\\nPublic marker forms:\\n\\n```text\\n[benny:bug]\\n[benny:bug] tracker=https://tracker.example/issue/123\\n[benny:performance]\\n[benny:performance] tracker=https://tracker.example/issue/123\\n[benny:other]\\n```\\n\\nProceed only for `bug` or `performance`. Capture the optional tracker URL. Stop silently for `other`, a missing verdict, an untrusted author, conflicting markers, or a timeout.\\n\\nThis marker replaces private bot identities and free-form verdict matching.\\n\\n## 3. Apply ownership and fix-artifact gates\\n\\nRe-read the thread immediately before starting work.\\n\\n### Someone is explicitly fixing it\\n\\nStop when a person clearly claims the fix, gives a concrete implementation plan, or asks another agent to implement, patch, fix, or open a pull request.\\n\\nDo not treat these as fix ownership:\\n\\n- A bot summarizes evidence.\\n- A tool looks up logs or tickets.\\n- Someone asks a bot to diagnose, explain, inspect, or reproduce.\\n- A bot posts a cause hypothesis without agreeing to implement it.\\n\\nJudge the requested action, not the presence of a bot.\\n\\n### A fix artifact already exists\\n\\nIf an open pull request or merged commit plausibly fixes this report, switch to `references/verify-existing-fix.md`.\\n\\nAn artifact may come from the thread, tracker issue, repository history, or pull request search. A claim without a commit or pull request is not a fix artifact.\\n\\nIf a person owns the work but has not produced an artifact, stop. Do not race them.\\n\\n## 4. Open an optional operations thread\\n\\nIf `slack.operations_channel_id` is configured, the coordinator may create one root status message there. Keep status text short:\\n\\n- Reproducing\\n- Could not reproduce\\n- Blocked\\n- Reproduced\\n- Verifying existing fix\\n- Attempting bounded fix\\n- Draft pull request opened\\n- Fix did not land\\n\\nPrefer configured session Slack actions. Never expose the token to a worker.\\n\\nIf no operations channel is configured, keep detailed status in the automation run output. Do not substitute a source-channel root message.\\n\\n## 5. Load and check the control adapter\\n\\nRead `references/control-adapter.md` and the completed map at `control.feature_map_path`, then invoke the skill named by `control.skill_name`.\\n\\nFind the feature-map section that matches the reported user path. Read it before driving the app. If no section covers the feature, mark the run blocked instead of inventing a path or selector.\\n\\nRequire all seven capabilities:\\n\\n1. Bring up the configured target app and test environment.\\n2. Navigate the mapped feature and exercise its documented states.\\n3. Drive the real UI with clicks, typing, keys, scrolling, drag, resize, or navigation.\\n4. Inspect state without mutating it.\\n5. Capture screenshots.\\n6. Start and stop a screen recording.\\n7. Clean up processes, sessions, profiles, and temporary data.\\n\\nIf the adapter is absent or any required capability is missing, mark the operations status as blocked and stop. Do not pretend a screenshot, unit test, state mutation, or source reading is a UI repro.\\n\\n## 6. Study the report\\n\\nRead the full source thread and tracker issue when present.\\n\\nCollect:\\n\\n- Exact action path\\n- Expected behavior\\n- Observed behavior\\n- Discriminating state where they diverge\\n- Frequency\\n- Version, environment, and platform\\n- Attachments and error signatures\\n- Candidate code area\\n\\nInspect screenshots and video. When independent workers are available and authorized, use read-only parallel workers for code history, test ideas, blast-radius mapping, and media review when useful. Each worker gets a narrow question and the Slack-write prohibition.\\n\\nUse pstack's `how` skill to trace the action through the repository. Use `why` for regression history and defensive code. Form competing cause hypotheses and identify evidence that would separate them.\\n\\n## 7. Reproduce\\n\\nBring up the target app through the control adapter.\\n\\nConfirm the correct app, workspace, account, data set, and feature state before acting. Use stable app markers. Do not rely on window order or a familiar title alone.\\n\\nDrive the reported path through real UI actions.\\n\\nBefore calling it reproduced:\\n\\n1. Name the correct final state.\\n2. Name the broken final state.\\n3. Reach the point where they diverge.\\n4. Observe the broken state.\\n5. Reset enough state to make the second attempt independent.\\n6. Repeat the same path and observe the same broken state again.\\n7. Cross-check a real state value when possible.\\n\\nAn expected dialog, loading state, or setup step is not the bug. Capture the final state that distinguishes correct from broken behavior.\\n\\nUse the configured repro budget. If the symptom does not reproduce within it, report a clean `Could not reproduce` outcome. If the environment cannot provide a required capability, report `Blocked` and state what was missing.\\n\\n## 8. Capture and review evidence\\n\\nFor a successful repro:\\n\\n- Record the full path through the symptom.\\n- Capture a screenshot of the broken final state.\\n- Save a short note with the exact steps and observed state.\\n- Keep artifacts in the configured temporary artifact directory.\\n\\nHave an available authorized read-only media reviewer answer one question. If unavailable, disclose sequential media review as reduced capability: does the evidence visibly show the discriminating broken state?\\n\\nIf the answer is no or uncertain, the repro is not confirmed. Capture better evidence or use `Could not reproduce`.\\n\\nPost detailed evidence only in the operations thread when configured. Keep the source update concise.\\n\\n## 9. Report the repro outcome\\n\\nUpdate the operations status first.\\n\\nFor `Could not reproduce` or `Blocked`, post nothing in the source thread. The operations thread or run output carries the result.\\n\\nFor a confirmed repro, run the source preflight and post at most one unprompted source reply:\\n\\n- Say the issue reproduced.\\n- Link the operations evidence thread when one exists.\\n- Include at most three short findings.\\n- Link the tracker issue when one exists.\\n- Do not ping an owner by default.\\n\\nAttach evidence only when the configured Slack action keeps it inside the same source thread and the organization's retention policy allows it.\\n\\nWait for the configured rejection window. If a person shows that the setup or interpretation was wrong, correct the repro once. Do not start the fix phase until the window closes without a valid rejection.\\n\\n## 10. Verify an existing fix\\n\\nWhen a fix artifact exists, follow `references/verify-existing-fix.md`.\\n\\nVerification must show the symptom on the baseline and its absence on the patched build. Both paths use the real UI twice.\\n\\nDo not edit the existing fix, add a competing patch, or open a replacement pull request.\\n\\n## 11. Qualify a bounded fix\\n\\nAttempt a fix only when all of these hold:\\n\\n- The outcome is a plain confirmed repro.\\n- Media review confirmed the broken final state.\\n- No existing fix artifact appeared.\\n- No person claimed the fix during the rejection window.\\n- Runtime evidence identifies the root cause.\\n- The likely change fits the configured fix budget and repository scope.\\n- The control adapter can run both baseline and patched builds.\\n\\nIf any condition fails, keep the repro report and stop without a pull request.\\n\\nWhen the gate passes, update operations status to `Attempting bounded fix`.\\n\\n## 12. Root-cause and implement\\n\\nThe coordinator owns every Slack post, the final diff review, commits, and the pull request.\\n\\nRead-only workers may:\\n\\n- Trace code and history\\n- Propose tests\\n- Map blast radius\\n- Review a diff\\n- Review media\\n\\nThey do not edit, run external writes, post status, or own the fix.\\n\\nA tightly scoped code edit may be delegated during this phase only when tool isolation removes Slack credentials and every Slack write action from that worker. Its prompt must still carry the explicit Slack-write ban. The coordinator reviews the edit and runs or verifies the required tests. If tool isolation is uncertain, keep the edit in the coordinator.\\n\\nConfirm the mechanism with runtime evidence. Eliminate competing hypotheses before editing.\\n\\nFix the root cause with the smallest justified change.\\n\\n- Invoke pstack's `tdd` skill when there is a cheap local test target, and write the failing test before the fix.\\n- State why TDD was skipped when the path is expensive, unclear, or integration-heavy.\\n- Keep unrelated cleanup out.\\n- Stop if the change grows beyond the configured effort or risk budget.\\n\\n## 13. Prove the fix\\n\\nKeep the original baseline evidence.\\n\\nOn the patched build:\\n\\n1. Run the same real UI path.\\n2. Repeat it twice.\\n3. Show that the broken state is gone.\\n4. Show the expected state in its place.\\n5. Capture an after recording and screenshot.\\n6. Cross-check the same real state value used for the baseline.\\n\\nA compile, unit test, code review, or plausible diff is not after evidence.\\n\\nRun focused tests, then smoke the blast radius around the changed behavior. Cover nearby states, inputs, permissions, platforms, and failure paths that the change could affect. Stop without a pull request if a regression remains.\\n\\n## 14. Open a draft pull request\\n\\nOnly after before-and-after proof:\\n\\n- Review the final diff for unrelated changes and secrets.\\n- Run the repository's required checks.\\n- Create small ordered commits when the repository workflow allows it.\\n- Open a draft pull request. Never merge or deploy from this workflow.\\n- Link the configured tracker issue using the tracker's supported pull request syntax.\\n- Use the configured public URL form, normally `https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/pull/{number}`.\\n- Include the repro steps, root cause, test result, before and after evidence, and blast-radius checks.\\n- Run the pull request text and all Slack updates through pstack's `unslop` skill.\\n\\nIf pull request creation fails, do not claim success. Keep the commit or branch state in the run output and mark operations status `Fix did not land`.\\n\\nOn success, mark operations status `Draft pull request opened` and post one concise reply in the operations thread with the linked pull request. Do not create a second source-channel root or unprompted source reply.\\n\\n## 15. Follow-ups and cleanup\\n\\nWatch the configured operations thread for one follow-up window.\\n\\n- Answer a direct question from evidence already gathered.\\n- Apply one concrete correction and rerun the repro once when it invalidates the setup.\\n- Stay out of human coordination and side chatter.\\n- Stop when asked.\\n\\nAlways call the control adapter's cleanup capability. Keep artifacts only as long as the configured retention policy allows.\\n\\nNormalize the exposed event payload before freezing coordinates. The template message_ts field maps to trigger.ts; thread_ts remains the root override. Verify the actual connector schema and source parent. Missing or ambiguous mappings block execution.\\n\\nSOURCE /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/automations/benny/skills/reproduce-and-fix-issues/references/control-adapter.md\\n# Control-adapter contract\\n\\nBenny does not know how to start or drive every app. The user must configure one control skill or adapter that implements this contract for the target app.\\n\\nSet its skill name in `control.skill_name`.\\n\\nSet the completed user-facing feature map path in `control.feature_map_path`. Copy and fill [`feature-map.example.md`](./feature-map.example.md) outside `automations/benny/` instead of editing the copied example.\\n\\nIf the skill, feature map, or a required capability is absent, ambiguous, or incomplete, repro and fix work must fail closed.\\n\\n## Required capabilities\\n\\n### Bring up\\n\\nStart the requested app revision in the requested test environment.\\n\\nInput:\\n\\n- Repository and revision\\n- Build or start mode\\n- Workspace, account, fixture, and feature-state requirements\\n- Artifact directory\\n- Completed feature-map path\\n\\nReturn:\\n\\n- Session identifier\\n- How the adapter confirmed the correct app and environment\\n- Stable app markers\\n- Running process or target details needed by later calls\\n- Any missing capability\\n\\nThe adapter must distinguish the target app from a similar window, shell, or production instance.\\n\\n### Drive UI\\n\\nPerform real user actions:\\n\\n- Click\\n- Type\\n- Press keys\\n- Scroll\\n- Drag\\n- Resize\\n- Navigate through app controls\\n\\nPrefer roles, labels, and stable selectors. Use coordinates only after a fresh screenshot.\\n\\nReturn each action and the observed state change.\\n\\nDo not set internal state, call hidden app methods, write directly to storage, or inject DOM changes to create the symptom.\\n\\n### Drive mapped features and states\\n\\nRead the relevant feature-map section before driving the app.\\n\\nThe adapter must expose ways to:\\n\\n- Navigate every mapped feature through the user-visible path.\\n- Invoke the adapter action names listed for that feature.\\n- Interact with default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, loading, empty, error, selected, open, expanded, and feature-specific states when they apply.\\n- Arrange a state through safe fixture data, permissions, flags, service responses, or supported test controls.\\n- Reset the feature for a second independent repro attempt.\\n- Capture the screenshot, video, and read-only cross-check named by the feature map.\\n\\nUse roles, accessible names, ARIA relationships, stable component markers, and purpose-named data attributes. Never use generated CSS or StyleX classes, dynamic hashes, child indexes, or brittle DOM position.\\n\\nArranging a precondition is not permission to inject the reported symptom. If a query changes state, it belongs in `drive UI` and must represent a real user action.\\n\\n### Screenshot\\n\\nCapture the current app state to a requested path.\\n\\nReturn:\\n\\n- File path\\n- Capture time\\n- App marker or window title\\n- Short description of what should be visible\\n\\nThe screenshot must show enough app chrome to prove that the correct app is under test.\\n\\n### Recording\\n\\nStart and stop a screen recording around the full repro path.\\n\\nReturn:\\n\\n- File path\\n- Start and stop times\\n- Captured window or region\\n- Whether audio or sensitive overlays were omitted\\n\\nThe recording must show the discriminating final state, not only setup or a loading screen.\\n\\n### Cleanup\\n\\nStop processes and sessions created by the adapter.\\n\\nRemove disposable:\\n\\n- Browser or app profiles\\n- Temporary workspaces\\n- Test accounts or fixtures when the adapter created them\\n- Debug ports and tunnels\\n- Captures past their retention window\\n\\nReturn what was stopped, removed, retained, or left for a person.\\n\\nCleanup must not delete user work.\\n\\n## Adapter behavior\\n\\nThe adapter must:\\n\\n- Report capabilities before the repro starts.\\n- Report which feature-map sections it can drive and which are blocked.\\n- Use the same environment inputs for baseline and patched builds.\\n- Surface startup failures as failures.\\n- Bound retries.\\n- Keep secrets out of logs and artifacts.\\n- Keep captures outside the repository.\\n- Support a fresh or reset state between the two repro attempts.\\n- Avoid production changes unless the user explicitly configured a safe test action.\\n\\n## Environment translation\\n\\nBefore declaring an environment block, restate the defect without platform-specific nouns and ask whether the same behavior can be tested safely in the available environment.\\n\\nExamples:\\n\\n- A named browser may mean any external browser.\\n- A named key may mean the configured shortcut.\\n- A named remote host may mean a delayed or disconnected remote target.\\n\\nUse a translated attempt only when it tests the same underlying behavior. Bring up the app.\\n2. Confirm the stable app marker.\\n3. Load one completed feature-map section.\\n4. Navigate to that feature through its user path.\\n5. Exercise one disposable state through mapped adapter actions.\\n6. Inspect the resulting state.\\n7. Capture a screenshot.\\n8. Record a short clip.\\n9. Read the relevant section before driving the app. Keep this map at the user point of view. Discover internals and current code paths at runtime instead of freezing them here.\\n\\nCopy this file outside `automations/benny/`, for example to `.benny/feature-map.md`, and set `control.feature_map_path` to the copy. Pack refreshes must not overwrite it.\\n\\n## Per-feature template\\n\\n### `<feature name>`\\n\\n`<one-line user-visible purpose>`\\n\\n#### How a user gets there\\n\\n- Click path: `<screen> -> <menu, tab, or panel> -> <control>`\\n- Keyboard shortcut: `<shortcut or none>`\\n\\n#### How the control adapter drives it\\n\\n- `<adapter action>` with `<inputs>` should `<visible result>`.\\n- Reset: `<how the adapter returns to a fresh state>`.\\n\\n#### Stable selectors\\n\\n- `<role and accessible name>`\\n- `<ARIA relationship>`\\n- `<data-component or purpose-named data attribute>`\\n\\nNever use generated CSS or StyleX classes, dynamic hashes, child indexes, or brittle DOM position.\\n\\n#### States to exercise\\n\\n- Default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled\\n- Loading, empty, error\\n- Selected, open, expanded\\n- `<relevant feature-specific variants>`\\n\\nMark states that do not apply.\\n\\n#### Preconditions and setup\\n\\n- Auth: `<account state>`\\n- Data: `<fixture>`\\n- Permissions: `<role>`\\n- Flags: `<flag or none>`\\n- Services: `<required availability>`\\n\\n#### Evidence and cross-check\\n\\n- Screenshot: `<app identity, feature, and discriminating state>`\\n- Video: `<entry path, interaction, and final state>`\\n- Cross-check: `<read-only state or value that confirms the UI>`\\n\\n#### Gotchas\\n\\n- `<known dead end or wrong surface>`\\n- `<safe environment translation>`\\n\\n## Fictional example\\n\\nThese features belong to a fictional task app. They are examples, not required Benny features.\\n\\n### Sign in\\n\\nLets a user enter the task app.\\n\\n#### How a user gets there\\n\\n- Open the app and choose `Sign in`. No shortcut.\\n\\n#### How the control adapter drives it\\n\\n- `open_app`, `click Sign in`, `fill credentials`, and `click Continue` should open the item list.\\n- Reset by signing out and clearing the disposable session.\\n\\n#### Stable selectors\\n\\n- Button `Sign in`, textboxes `Email` and `Password`, `data-component=\\\"sign-in-form\\\"`\\n\\n#### States to exercise\\n\\n- Default, focus-visible, submitting, disabled, loading, error\\n\\n#### Preconditions and setup\\n\\n- Disposable account and available authentication service\\n\\n#### Evidence and cross-check\\n\\n- Record landing page through item list. Check read-only session state.\\n\\n#### Gotchas\\n\\n- A marketing page is the wrong surface. A missing auth service is a block.\\n\\n### Item list and detail\\n\\nLets a user browse items and open one.\\n\\n#### How a user gets there\\n\\n- Open the `Items` tab, then choose a row.\\n\\n#### How the control adapter drives it\\n\\n- `select_tab Items` and `click <fixture item>` should open its detail.\\n- Reset by closing the detail and clearing selection.\\n\\n#### Stable selectors\\n\\n- Tab and list named `Items`, fixture-named row, `data-component=\\\"item-detail\\\"`\\n\\n#### States to exercise\\n\\n- Loading, empty, error, selected, open, expanded\\n\\n#### Preconditions and setup\\n\\n- Named fixture items, read permission, available item service\\n\\n#### Evidence and cross-check\\n\\n- Show selection and matching detail title. Check selected-item ID.\\n\\n#### Gotchas\\n\\n- Search results may look similar but use a different path.\\n\\n### Item editor\\n\\nLets a user create or edit an item.\\n\\n#### How a user gets there\\n\\n- Choose `Edit` from detail or `New item` from the list.\\n\\n#### How the control adapter drives it\\n\\n- `click Edit`, `fill <field>`, and `click Save` should update detail.\\n- Reset by restoring the fixture.\\n\\n#### Stable selectors\\n\\n- Buttons `Edit`, `New item`, `Save`, form `Item editor`, label-linked fields\\n\\n#### States to exercise\\n\\n- Default, focus-visible, dirty, validating, disabled, saving, error, success\\n\\n#### Preconditions and setup\\n\\n- Editable fixture, write permission, available save service\\n\\n#### Evidence and cross-check\\n\\n- Show field change through updated detail. Check the stored item value read-only.\\n\\n#### Gotchas\\n\\n- Do not inject form state. A read-only detail field is not the editor.\\n\\n### Settings\\n\\nLets a user change personal preferences.\\n\\n#### How a user gets there\\n\\n- Open the profile menu, then choose `Settings`.\\n\\n#### How the control adapter drives it\\n\\n- `open_menu Profile`, `click Settings`, and `toggle <preference>` should update the control.\\n- Reset by restoring the starting preference.\\n\\n#### Stable selectors\\n\\n- Button `Profile`, menu item `Settings`, region `Settings`, purpose-named preference attribute\\n\\n#### States to exercise\\n\\n- Closed, open, selected, focus-visible, disabled, loading, error\\n\\n#### Preconditions and setup\\n\\n- Signed-in test account, known preferences, available preference service\\n\\n#### Evidence and cross-check\\n\\n- Show the menu path and final control state. Check the preference value read-only.\\n\\n#### Gotchas\\n\\n- Operating-system settings are a different surface.\\n\\n## Completeness checklist\\n\\n- Every reproducible user-facing feature has a section.\\n- Every section names a user path, adapter actions, and reset.\\n- Selectors use roles, names, ARIA, stable component markers, or purpose-named attributes.\\n- No selector uses generated classes or DOM position.\\n- Relevant interaction, loading, empty, error, selected, and expanded states are covered.\\n- Auth, fixtures, permissions, flags, and services are explicit.\\n- Screenshot, video, and underlying cross-check requirements are explicit.\\n- Wrong surfaces, dead ends, and safe environment translations are listed.\\n- Implementation details remain runtime discoveries.\\n\\nSOURCE /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/automations/benny/skills/reproduce-and-fix-issues/references/verify-existing-fix.md\\n# Verify an existing fix\\n\\nUse this mode when an open pull request or merged commit plausibly fixes the report.\\n\\nThe existing artifact owns the fix. Verify it. Do not edit it, author a competing patch, or open another pull request.\\n\\n## Qualify the artifact\\n\\nRequire one concrete artifact:\\n\\n- An open pull request with code changes that address the symptom\\n- A merged pull request\\n- A merged commit with matching code and intent\\n\\nA thread claim, tracker status, branch name, or cause hypothesis without a pull request or commit is not enough.\\n\\nWhen several artifacts exist, choose the one linked from the source thread or tracker. Otherwise choose the closest match to the affected code and state why.\\n\\n## Protect the working tree\\n\\nUse an isolated worktree or another clean checkout when the repository supports it. Do not overwrite user changes.\\n\\nRecord:\\n\\n- Baseline revision\\n- Patched revision\\n- Pull request or commit URL\\n- Build and environment inputs shared by both runs\\n\\nUse regular `github.com` pull request links.\\n\\n## Measure the baseline\\n\\nFor an open pull request, use its base branch as the baseline.\\n\\nFor a merged fix, use the revision immediately before the fix when that revision builds and represents the old behavior.\\n\\nThrough the configured control adapter:\\n\\n1. Bring up the baseline app.\\n2. Confirm the correct app and environment.\\n3. Run the reported path through real UI actions.\\n4. Observe the discriminating symptom.\\n5. Reset and repeat it.\\n6. Capture baseline recording, screenshot, and state check.\\n\\nIf the symptom does not appear twice on the baseline, there is no baseline. Do not claim that the fix works.\\n\\n## Measure the patched build\\n\\nBuild and run the pull request or fix commit with the same environment and data.\\n\\n1. Run the same UI path.\\n2. Repeat it twice.\\n3. Confirm that the broken state is gone.\\n4. Confirm the expected state appears.\\n5. Capture after recording, screenshot, and the same state check.\\n\\nDo not stop at compilation or tests. The after result must come from a running patched app.\\n\\n## Outcomes\\n\\n### Confirmed\\n\\nThe baseline reproduces twice and the patched build resolves it twice.\\n\\n- Mark operations status as verified.\\n- Link the artifact.\\n- Post one concise source-thread reply after the source preflight.\\n- Include the before and after result.\\n- Open no pull request.\\n\\n### Insufficient fix\\n\\nThe symptom appears on both baseline and patched builds.\\n\\n- Mark operations status as reproduced but not fixed.\\n- Link the artifact and say it did not resolve the symptom.\\n- Post the normal confirmed-repro source update if the run has not already used it.\\n- Open no competing pull request.\\n\\n### Inconclusive\\n\\nThe baseline does not reproduce, the patched app cannot run, or the evidence does not show the discriminating state.\\n\\n- Do not claim success.\\n- State which half could not be measured.\\n- Keep the result in the operations thread or run output.\\n- Post nothing in the source thread unless a direct question requires an answer.\\n\\n## Cleanup\\n\\nStop both builds, remove temporary profiles and captures according to retention policy, and return the repository to its prior state without discarding user work.\\n\\nRepository checkout changes and adapter execution require authorized isolated test scope. Message and status writes need separate destination authorization. If unavailable, retain the verification plan locally and report blocked.
