Use when installing Benny or changing its Slack, tracker, repository, routing, control, model, or budget settings.\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Set up Benny\\n\\nBenny ships as a dormant automation pack inside pstack. The plugin manifest exposes only pstack's normal skill root; this file and the two operational files are not slash skills.\\n\\nThe human enters setup by pointing the host at the pack's `FOR_AGENTS.md`. The bootstrap flow copies the whole pack into the target repository, then reads this file directly at `automations/benny/skills/setup-benny/REFERENCE.md`.\\n\\nBenny needs external configuration and two live host-supported automations.\\n\\nDo not create or update an automation until the user explicitly asks. Never put a secret value in plugin files, prompts, or committed configuration.\\n\\n## 1. Copy the pack and verify shared pstack skills\\n\\nDo this before asking for Benny configuration and before invoking an authorized automation creation capability. Copying to another repository requires explicit authorization.\\n\\nAsk which repository will run the automations. The source pack is the directory containing `FOR_AGENTS.md`. The destination is `<target-repository>/automations/benny/`.\\n\\nMerge the entire source pack into the destination:\\n\\n1. With explicit copy authorization, create the destination when it is absent.\\n2. Copy every source file to the same relative path.\\n3. Preserve destination-only files. Never delete unrelated files during install or refresh.\\n4. Keep user-owned configuration, feature maps, and routing maps outside the destination. Never overwrite them.\\n5. When an existing source-managed file differs, inspect the diff and merge without discarding local edits. If ownership is ambiguous, stop and ask before replacing it.\\n6. Verify that the destination contains `FOR_AGENTS.md`, this setup file, both operational files, their references, and the templates.\\n\\nIf this file is already being read from the target destination, treat the copy as complete and run the same verification before continuing.\\n\\nDo not write host settings, install plugins, or enable shared dependencies automatically. If the target cannot load the verified package dependencies, report setup-required and wait for separately authorized host setup.\\n\\nReload the target project or start a fresh agent rooted there. Verify that these shared pstack skills resolve from project scope:\\n\\n- `how`\\n- `why`\\n- `tdd`\\n- `unslop`\\n- `principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state`\\n- `principle-minimize-reader-load`\\n- `principle-guard-the-context-window`\\n- `principle-sequence-verifiable-units`\\n- `principle-fix-root-causes`\\n- `principle-prove-it-works`\\n\\nDo not count a skill loaded from the current session or a user-scoped plugin. The check must show that a fresh agent in the target repository receives the verified pstack dependencies.\\n\\nIf project-scoped plugin installation is unavailable or any shared dependency does not resolve, stop and explain the failure.\\n\\nThe Benny files are read directly from `automations/benny/`. Do not add that directory to a plugin manifest or expect its `REFERENCE.md` files to appear in the slash-skill list.\\n\\nTell the user that `automations/benny/` and any referenced secret-free configuration must be committed before either automation is enabled. Do not commit them unless the user asks.\\n\\nOnce this check passes, live automation prompts may read the committed operational files by their stable repository-relative paths. They must not embed a plugin cache path or copy the file contents.\\n\\n## 2. Adapt the configuration\\n\\nOpen these copied examples:\\n\\n- `../../templates/configuration.example.yaml`\\n- `../reproduce-and-fix-issues/references/feature-map.example.md`\\n\\nCreate user-owned copies outside `automations/benny/`. These are configuration files, not pack files. Example locations:\\n\\n- Project config, such as `.benny/configuration.yaml`\\n- Project feature map, such as `.benny/feature-map.md`\\n- Project routing map, such as `.benny/routing.md`\\n- User config, such as `~/.config/benny/configuration.yaml`\\n- User feature map, such as `~/.config/benny/feature-map.md`\\n\\nFill one feature-map section for every user-facing feature the automation may reproduce. Keep it at the user point of view. Do not freeze implementation details or current code paths in the map.\\n\\nDo not edit the copied examples. Pack refreshes may update source-managed files after conflict review, but they must never touch the user-owned copies.\\n\\nPrefer committed, secret-free files in the target repository when a fresh automation checkout must read them. Otherwise paraphrase the required values into the live prompt. Reference a repository file only after repository inspection confirms that the file is committed in the repository where the automation runs.\\n\\nUse stable repository-relative paths for committed pack and configuration files. Never reference the plugin source directory or a plugin cache path from a live automation.\\n\\n## 3. Fill the required choices\\n\\nAsk for or confirm:\\n\\n- Source Slack channel ID\\n- Optional operations or status channel ID\\n- Repository URL and default branch\\n- Triage identity or Slack user ID\\n- Issue tracker type, team, project, labels, and intake status\\n- Tracker adapter skill or MCP actions\\n- Optional routing map path\\n- Required control skill name\\n- Required user-facing feature-map path\\n- Status emoji strings\\n- Pull request URL format\\n- Polling and effort budgets\\n- Model slug for triage, repro, code work, and media review\\n\\nUse only model slugs shown as available in the session's observed model enumeration or current supported model list. Do not guess a slug and do not carry over a private default.\\n\\nThe source channel, triage identity, repository, tracker adapter, control skill, and feature map must be explicit. Fail setup if any required value stays ambiguous.\\n\\nUse pstack's `unslop` skill on the final automation names, descriptions, and prompt shims before saving them.\\n\\n## 4. Check integration capabilities\\n\\nThe triage automation needs:\\n\\n- Read access to the configured source Slack channel and its threads\\n- Thread-reply access in that channel\\n- Attachment metadata and file download access when reports include media\\n- Search, read, create, and update access through the configured issue-tracker adapter\\n\\nThe repro automation needs:\\n\\n- Read access to the source thread\\n- Thread-reply access in the source channel\\n- Optional post and edit access in the configured operations channel\\n- Repository read and history access\\n- A pull request action that can open a draft pull request\\n- The configured control-adapter skill\\n\\nPrefer configured session Slack actions for reads and posts. The optional `BENNY_SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` may fill a narrow gap such as editing one operations status message or downloading an attachment. Store the value in a secret manager or environment, not in YAML.\\n\\nDo not use undocumented integration endpoints.\\n\\n## 5. Prepare the routing map\\n\\nIf the user wants reroutes or owner pings:\\n\\n1. Copy `../triage-issue-reports/references/routing.example.md` outside `automations/benny/`.\\n2. Replace every placeholder with public or organization-local values.\\n3. Keep owner pings off by default.\\n4. Allow a ping only for a configured feature owner or a confirmed likely regression author.\\n\\nIf no routing map is configured, triage may classify a report but must not guess a destination or owner.\\n\\n## 6. Verify the control adapter\\n\\nRead `../reproduce-and-fix-issues/references/control-adapter.md` and the user's completed feature map.\\n\\nUsing supplied or inert evidence first, confirm that the named skill declares it can:\\n\\n- Bring up the target app\\n- Navigate every mapped feature through the real UI\\n- Exercise mapped states through declared adapter actions\\n- Inspect state without forcing the result\\n- Capture screenshots\\n- Start and stop a recording\\n- Clean up its processes and temporary data\\n\\nIf any capability is missing, leave the repro automation disabled. It must fail closed rather than claim a reproduction it did not perform.\\n\\n## 7. Prepare the live automations\\n\\nAsk whether this is first-time creation or configuration of existing automations.\\n\\nRead `../../FOR_AGENTS.md` from the copied pack as the primary user-intent source for either path. Use it to understand the two triggers, tools, instructions, outcomes, and shared rules.\\n\\n### First-time creation\\n\\nCreate one automation at a time.\\n\\nFor each automation:\\n\\n1. Read the matching copied prompt template as secondary internal source material.\\n2. Turn `FOR_AGENTS.md`, the finished Benny configuration, and the template intent into a complete natural-language request.\\n3. Tell the live prompt to read and follow its exact committed operational file under `automations/benny/`.\\n4. Use the stable repository-relative path, not a plugin source or cache path. Do not copy the operational file contents into the live prompt.\\n5. Bind the exposed automation creation capability and check its current supported trigger types. Missing event support blocks setup.\\n6. Let the authorized host workflow discover Slack channels, the repository, and connected integrations.\\n7. Freeze source coordinates\\n\\nBefore making a work list or delegating:\\n\\n1. Read `source_channel_id` from the trigger.\\n2. Require it to equal the configured source channel.\\n3. Fetch a stable source permalink.\\n\\nEvery later source read and post must use those stored values. Never replace them with a reply timestamp or an operations-thread timestamp.\\n\\n## 2. Read the whole report\\n\\nRead the root and current replies before deciding.\\n\\nCapture:\\n\\n- Reporter wording\\n- Product version, app build, environment, and platform when present\\n- Expected behavior\\n- Observed behavior\\n- Frequency and trigger\\n- Error text or stack signature\\n- Existing issue, commit, or pull request links\\n- Any explicit statement that someone is already fixing it\\n\\nInspect every relevant attachment.\\n\\n- Read screenshots at full useful resolution.\\n- Review video for the state transition that separates correct and broken behavior.\\n- Read logs, traces, and crash text for concrete signatures.\\n- If media needs specialist review, use an available authorized read-only media worker and ask a narrow question. The worker returns findings only.\\n- If an attachment cannot be read, say so in the verdict. Do not invent what it shows.\\n\\nUse evidence already in the thread before asking the reporter for more.\\n\\n## 3. Trace cause before routing\\n\\nDo a bounded source and history pass before choosing an owner or destination. Use pstack's `how` skill to trace the path from the reported action to the observed result. Use `why` when the report looks like a regression or touches defensive code.\\n\\n1. Identify the likely code path from the reported action to the observed result.\\n2. Check whether the visible symptom belongs to that code path or a dependency below it.\\n3. Check recent changes when the report looks like a regression.\\n4. Check whether a merged commit or open pull request already addresses the same symptom.\\n5. Separate confirmed facts from hypotheses.\\n\\nThis pass does not need a complete root cause. It must be strong enough to avoid routing a visible symptom to the wrong owner.\\n\\nIf the repository cannot be read, do not guess a code owner. Continue with a conservative classification and say that cause tracing was unavailable.\\n\\n## 4. Classify\\n\\nChoose one category.\\n\\n### Bug\\n\\nSomething violates intended behavior. Examples include wrong output, broken state, an error, a crash, a hang, a silent no-op, or a regression.\\n\\n### Performance\\n\\nThe report describes measurable slowness, excess memory, battery drain, jank, or another resource problem. Treat it as a bug, but preserve measurements and profiles.\\n\\n### Feature request\\n\\nThe current behavior appears intentional and the reporter wants a different behavior or affordance.\\n\\n### Question or feedback\\n\\nThe report asks how something works, expresses a preference without a concrete defect, or gives general feedback.\\n\\n### Reroute\\n\\nCause tracing shows that another configured destination owns the issue.\\n\\nWhen the bug versus feature line is unclear, do not file. The one verdict may ask one focused question and use the `other` marker.\\n\\n## 5. Apply configured routing\\n\\nRead the optional routing map from `routing.map_path`.\\n\\n- Match on confirmed product area, code path, or error signature.\\n- A visible symptom alone is not enough when cause tracing points elsewhere.\\n- If no route matches, say the owner is unclear. Do not guess.\\n- Do not cross-post. Tell the reporter where to take the issue in the source thread.\\n\\nOwner pings are off by default. A ping is allowed only when all of these hold:\\n\\n1. The routing map explicitly names the owner.\\n2. The config allows that ping type.\\n3. The item is a feature request that needs owner input, or recent history identifies a likely regression author with strong evidence.\\n4. The owner is not a broad on-call group.\\n\\nNo other case gets a ping.\\n\\n## 6. Use the issue-tracker adapter\\n\\nThe tracker is an adapter, not a required vendor. A Linear adapter is one valid example. A GitHub Issues adapter or another tracker may implement the same contract.\\n\\nThe configured adapter must provide:\\n\\n- Search issues by text, state, label, source URL, and date range\\n- Read one issue and its links\\n- Create an issue with title, body, status, labels, and source URL\\n- Update an existing issue without replacing unrelated fields\\n- Add a source link and recurrence note\\n- Cancel, close, or delete an issue created by this run if the Slack handoff fails\\n\\nIf a required operation is unavailable, fail closed for that write.\\n\\nResolve configured team, project, status, and labels at runtime. Do not invent IDs, create labels, assign owners, or set priority unless the config explicitly requires it.\\n\\n## 7. Dedupe\\n\\nAlways check whether this source permalink is already linked to a tracker issue or a prior triage reply. If so, do not post or create a duplicate.\\n\\nFor bugs and performance reports, search the tracker using:\\n\\n- Exact error or crash signature\\n- Product area\\n- Trigger\\n- Symptom\\n- Version or date window\\n- Suspected regression commit\\n- Source permalink\\n\\nChoose one outcome:\\n\\n- Confident duplicate: same signature, or the same area, trigger, and symptom, or a confirmed shared cause.\\n- Possibly related: a shared cause is plausible but not proven.\\n- Weak resemblance: similarity is superficial.\\n- No match.\\n\\nFor a confident duplicate, update the existing issue with the source permalink and one short recurrence note. Do not reopen, relabel, or reassign it unless the config says to.\\n\\nFor a possible match, link it in the verdict as uncertain and create nothing.\\n\\nA long-closed issue is a regression lead, not automatically a live duplicate.\\n\\n## 8. Decide whether to create\\n\\nCreate only when all of these are true:\\n\\n1. The classification is bug or performance.\\n2. The behavior is clearly broken.\\n3. The issue is still live or not known to be fixed.\\n4. Dedupe found no confident or plausible live match.\\n5. The source parent and permalink passed preflight.\\n6. The tracker target fields resolved.\\n7. The adapter can compensate if the verdict post fails.\\n\\nNever create for a feature request, question, feedback item, reroute, possible duplicate, confident duplicate, or already-fixed issue.\\n\\nThe new issue must be self-contained:\\n\\n- Plain title that names the area and symptom\\n- Reporter quote\\n- Expected and observed behavior\\n- Version and environment, or `unknown`\\n- Trigger and frequency\\n- Source thread permalink\\n- Short cause-tracing findings with hypotheses labeled as hypotheses\\n- Inline screenshot or representative video frame when supported\\n- Links to remaining artifacts\\n- Configured intake status and labels\\n\\nDo not put a guessed root cause in the title.\\n\\n## 9. Spawn three parallel review subagents over the active transcript, surface learnings, and route each to a concrete edit on an existing skill. Use when the user says reflect.\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Reflect\\n\\nMine the current conversation for durable learnings, then route them into skill edits.\\n\\n## When to invoke\\n\\nInvoke when the user says \\\"reflect\\\" or \\\"/reflect\\\". Skip when the conversation is trivial, off-topic, or already covered by an existing skill the parent followed correctly. One-offs are not learnings.\\n\\n## Process\\n\\n### 1. Locate the active transcript\\n\\nThe parent discovers the active session through authorized exposed history or file tools. Read [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md), [assignment contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md), and [workflow ownership](../../references/workflow-ownership.md). Record observed read, history, spawn, result inspection, execution and write bindings as applicable. Preserve the active controller.\\n\\nUse only the transcript location supplied for this active workspace or an exposed active-chat reference. Verify its opening user prompt before use. Do not search unrelated workspace or user chat directories. If no active transcript resolves, write a tight session digest, mark its omissions, and pass that instead. If neither authorized history nor a usable digest exists, stop with blocked evidence-backed reflection.\\n\\n### 2. Spawn three reviewers in parallel\\n\\nWhen authorized independent workers are exposed, assign three reviewers in parallel under the assignment contract. Give each an immutable revision, role, separate output ownership and the complete corresponding template. Reviewers may read transcript-referenced context through available authorized tools but may not write code, edit skills, commit or send messages.\\n\\n| Lens | Selection role | Prompt template |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Judgment | reflect judgment, divergent, synthesizer | [judgment reviewer](references/judgment-reviewer.md) |\\n| Tooling | reflect tooling | [tooling reviewer](references/tooling-reviewer.md) |\\n| Divergent | reflect judgment, divergent, synthesizer | [divergent reviewer](references/divergent-reviewer.md) |\\n\\nUse the model-role contract for each selection role. Honor an explicitly supplied authorized role preference only when its model and effort are currently supported; otherwise retain inherit-parent and disclose the limit. Record requested and observed values separately. A rejected choice requires disclosed supported fallback or a block when the exact choice is required. Different role prompts do not establish model diversity.\\n\\nPass each template in full, substituting the transcript path or digest where marked. Inspect every worker result and its artifacts; a completion notification is insufficient. If independent workers are unavailable, perform the same three lens passes sequentially as reduced capability, followed by synthesis. Do not claim independent review.\\n\\n### 3. Synthesize\\n\\nAssign an independent synthesizer under the same capability, model-role and assignment contracts when available. Give it the [synthesizer template](references/synthesizer.md) in full with each reviewer's full output inlined where marked. Its spot-verification uses only authorized transcript-referenced context reads. Inspect its result. In the reduced sequential branch, apply the same synthesis prompt after all three lens passes. The synthesizer returns a structured Accepted / Rejected / Backlog list.\\n\\n### 4. Structural enforcement check\\n\\nSanity-check the synthesizer's Accepted list. For any item that would be enforced more reliably by a lint rule, script, metadata flag, or runtime check, move it from Accepted to Backlog. See the [encode lessons in structure principle](../principle-encode-lessons-in-structure/SKILL.md).\\n\\n### 5. Apply\\n\\nBefore applying any Accepted edit, present the synthesizer's full Accepted/Rejected/Backlog output to the user and wait for explicit approval. The user picks which subset to apply and may redirect routings. Skill changes affect future agents that load the changed skill. Do not auto-apply.\\n\\nFile Backlog items to the team devex tracker only when the user has explicitly authorized that tracker write and the exposed tool permits it. Otherwise provide an unfiled Backlog draft and state the limit. Backlog filing never authorizes Accepted edits.\\n\\nFor each approved Accepted item, follow the Routing field exactly:\\n\\n- Trivial existing-skill edit (a one-line bullet, a tightened sentence, a stale fact corrected): parent does directly.\\n- Substantive existing-skill edit (a new section, a new pattern table, more than ~10 lines): hand to an available authorized skill-authoring workflow and run its draft / test / iterate loop.\\n- `tune description: <skill path>` (the skill exists but didn't trigger when it should have): hand to that skill-authoring workflow and run its description-optimization loop.\\n- `new skill via create-skill: <kebab-name>`: hand creation to that skill-authoring workflow. Do not invent the shape ad hoc.\\n\\nIf a required authoring workflow is unavailable, keep the approved proposal as a draft and report application blocked. Do not claim its draft / test / iterate or description-optimization loop ran.\\n\\nIf your environment ships an authorized SKILL.md validator, run it on every touched skill before declaring done. Skip this step if it doesn't.\\n\\n### 6. Summarize for the user\\n\\nShort list, no preamble:\\n\\n- Edits applied: `<skill path>`. What changed, one line each.\\n- New skills created: `<skill path>`. One line each (rare).\\n- Backlog filed to the devex tracker: `<issue title>` (`<tags>`). One line each.\\n- Dropped: one line per rejected finding + reason from the synthesizer.\\n\\nSOURCE /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/reflect/references/divergent-reviewer.md\\nYou are a reviewer applying the divergent lens to a session transcript. Your strength is divergent angles and blind-spot coverage. The things the other reviewers will miss. Second-order effects. What didn't happen but should have. Anti-patterns avoided. Alternative paths not taken.\\n\\nLook for the contrarian framing. If two reviewers will probably surface principle X, find the principle Y that complicates or contradicts X. The session's \\\"obvious\\\" learning is rarely the most useful one. Find the one beneath it.\\n\\nDo not modify files in the repo. Use any available authorized read tool in your environment (e.g. a ticket tracker, chat, docs, observability, error tracker, source control) to look up context referenced in the transcript. Singletons must clear a higher bar on the other criteria.\\n- Decision-changing: a future agent does something different because of the edit, not just reads more text.\\n- Structural-mechanism check: route to Backlog when a lint rule, script, metadata flag, or runtime check already enforces the rule or could enforce it cheaply. Bun.file(b+\\\\\\\"skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/orchestrate.md\\\\\\\").text());'\\\"\",\"aggregated_output\":\"# Workflow ownership\\n\\nAn explicit pstack invocation gives pstack ownership of that workflow. An explicit Superpowers invocation gives Superpowers ownership. Do not run both controllers over the same assignment or let one silently replace the other's plan, review, or integration decisions.\\n\\nFor an unqualified request, D1 retains the already active workflow. With no active workflow, use host defaults and do not activate either orchestration mode automatically. If both pstack and Superpowers are explicitly requested, clarify ownership before launching workers or changing artifacts. Preserve the active controller across follow-ups unless the user changes ownership. A helper skill can advise the owner without becoming a second controller.\\n\\nThe owner assigns one coordinator. Workers produce isolated artifacts and evidence; the coordinator reviews and integrates them. Shared inventory and registry writes belong to the coordinator. Worker cancellation, stale results or unavailable tools do not transfer that ownership automatically.\\n\\nHost permissions and user authorization constrain every owner. Local structural tests, documented APIs and declared cases provide no host pass. Explicit reduced or blocked results remain visible beside the full expectation.\\n\\n---\\nname: principle-encode-lessons-in-structure\\ndescription: \\\"Apply when you catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time, or notice a recurring correction. Encode the rule as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Encode Lessons in Structure\\n\\nEncode recurring fixes in mechanisms (tools, code, metadata, automation) instead of textual instructions. Every error, human correction, and unexpected outcome is a learning signal. Capture it, route it, and close the loop.\\n\\n**Why:** Textual instructions are easy to miss. They require the reader to notice, remember, and comply. Structural mechanisms (lint rules, metadata flags, runtime checks, automation scripts) enforce the rule without cooperation.\\n\\n**Pattern:**\\nWhen you catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time:\\n1. Ask: can this be a lint rule, a metadata flag, a runtime check, or a script?\\n2. If yes, encode it. Delete the instruction\\n3. If no (requires judgment), make the instruction more prominent and add an example of the failure mode\\n\\n**Pick the strongest mechanism.** When more than one mechanism would work, choose the strongest the situation allows (an unrepresentable state that cannot compile, then a lint or banned API that fails CI, then a canonical helper, then a runtime check), because agents copy whatever the surrounding code already does and a weaker guard becomes the next template.\\n\\n**Corollary:** If the fix is structural, only use the structural fix. The instruction is the symptom.\\n\\n**Feedback loop:**\\n- **Capture every correction.** When the human intervenes or tests fail, decide if it's a one-off or a pattern.\\n- **Route to the right layer.** One-off -> brain note. Recurring fix -> skill or lint rule. Systemic issue -> principle.\\n- **Close the loop.** Don't just record. Apply now or create a concrete todo.\\n\\n**Anti-patterns:**\\n- Acknowledging without recording (\\\"I'll keep that in mind\\\" does not persist)\\n- Recording without routing (a brain note about a lint rule that should exist is wasted unless the lint rule gets implemented)\\n- Fixing without generalizing (fixing one instance while leaving the recurring pattern intact)\\n\\n## Session capabilities and authorization\\n\\nFollow [session capability discovery](../../references/host-capabilities.md) for reads, writes, execution and durable persistence. Apply mechanisms within the authorized task. This principle does not authorize installation, global settings or external actions. Treat a brain note as an authorized durable record when persistence is available; claim it saved only after write and readback. If persistence is unavailable, state that limit and include the concrete todo in the current response.\\n\\nIf writes or execution are unavailable, provide a reduced proposal that names the check, its integration point and the remaining implementation or verification work. If the rule or source needed to select a mechanism is missing, identify the missing inputs and keep the proposal provisional. Delete a redundant instruction only once the structural fix enforces its rule. Preserve judgment-dependent guidance with a prominent failure example.\\n\\nPreserve explicit-invocation metadata without assuming the host enforces it. Claim enforcement, implementation or verification only for observed operations.\\n\\n### Orchestrate\\n\\nRead [poteto-mode](../SKILL.md), [capabilities](../../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../../references/model-roles.md), [assignment contract](../../../references/orchestration-contract.md), [workflow ownership](../../../references/workflow-ownership.md), and the [poteto role prompt](../../../references/agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md) in full. This playbook responds to \\\"run this whole project\\\" and \\\"own this migration until it lands\\\". Aliases do not register host commands. Read applied principles and routed skills before dependent work. Use [arena](../../arena/SKILL.md), [figure-it-out](../../figure-it-out/SKILL.md), [show-me-your-work](../../show-me-your-work/SKILL.md), [separate shared state](../../principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state/SKILL.md), and [encode lessons](../../principle-encode-lessons-in-structure/SKILL.md) where the steps call for them. Apply [unslop](../../unslop/SKILL.md) to briefs and reports.\\n\\nA program needs observed independent worker operations, isolated ownership, execution, persistence and result inspection. Without workers, authorized sequential work is reduced capability and cannot satisfy a required independent review or standing program. Without execution or writable persistence, block helper-dependent work and offer a scoped read-only handoff. Missing wake or remote placement means foreground operation only. Recurring wakes need explicit scheduling authorization. No unattended continuity is implied. Commits, pushes, PR creation, merges, messages, deployments, deletion and setup each retain their applicable permission gates. Gate defaults never grant permission by silence.\\n\\nThe companion wake mechanism is a host capability, not a bundled loop skill. Pending caller paths are `playbooks/autonomous-run.md` and `playbooks/babysit.md`. Stop dependent routes that need those instructions until they exist. The embedded small-task collapse in Frame remains usable without the Autonomous run document. Never install missing companions implicitly.\\n\\n**You own the program, never the code. Author briefs, drain the queue, keep the frontier green, decide.** For a whole project handed to one standing coordinator chat: multi-day, many stacked PRs, dozens to hundreds of subagents, the human checking in twice a day instead of every five minutes. One task driven to a predicate is Autonomous run. One ambitious run needing a bespoke workflow is figure-it-out. Route here when the work outlives any single agent. Work one agent could finish inside the session's budget is not a program.\\n\\nCeremony must scale with the program. On cheap near-identical units, collapse it as each section directs.\\n\\nThe following rules govern the program.\\n\\n- Completions are queue events, not interrupts.\\n- Every spawn and every resume carries the standing orders verbatim.\\n- The brief is the product. A vague brief fails quietly, because a worker cannot ask you a question.\\n\\n#### Roles and placement\\n\\n- **Coordinator (this chat).** Local. Frames, authors briefs, drains the inbox, owns the human report, makes judgment calls. It never authors or edits code. Conflicted merges, restacks, and code changes are always tasks. Mechanically landing a verified unit (fast-forward or clean cherry-pick of a worker's commit, then push) is bookkeeping the coordinator may do itself on repos where local git is cheap. Queueing finished work behind an idle stacker is how a deadline harvests nothing. Bind spawn, follow-up, wait, result inspection and stop to exposed authorized operations. State reads and writes go through the bookkeeping helper at drain points. Most compact outputs are bounded summaries; inbox drain returns all pointers, status returns three lines, and `--json` returns complete rows. The CLI never spawns, waits, or wakes anything.\\n- **Sub-coordinator.** Always local, durable, one per track, and only when the program exceeds what one coordinator's drains can manage. A track the coordinator can drain itself needs no middle layer. Each nested layer re-pays a full orientation preamble, and a blocking sub-coordinator hides its children while the parent idles. Owns its track's units and boards, authors its workers' briefs, spawns its own workers and verifiers only when nesting and isolation are exposed and observed. Depth 3 is the desired ceiling, not a portable runtime guarantee. Rolls up aggregates at wave boundaries. Never forwards raw child reports. Cap in-flight children at what one drain can process, roughly ten, as a rolling window. Never as blocking batches, which cost the slowest child of every batch.\\n- **Worker / verifier.** Prefer remote workers when exposed and authorized. Local-only verification, this run's accessible transcripts, simulators, local IDE state and local auth require a suitable local binding. Discover control-ui and control-cli companions rather than assuming them. Remote workers cannot be assumed to read the local store, so inline required context or use paths confirmed readable by that worker. Prefer fewer, broader workers. One writer per worktree or branch (principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state). Prefer a verifier on a different observed model family. Inherit the parent selection unless explicit supported selection is observed. Unknown actual models leave diversity unverified; an unavailable required family blocks that gate.\\n\\nDepth stays at coordinator, track, worker. Author the track decomposition per project (build, landing, and verification are common cuts, not a required shape). Hard-coded swarm trees were tried and parked as too rigid.\\n\\n#### Store layout\\n\\nChoose an explicitly authorized task-owned writable `orchestrate/<project-slug>/` outside the package tree. Every file has exactly one writer. Owners publish facts, readers aggregate at read time. Use `bun --no-install <package-root>/skills/poteto-mode/scripts/orch/orch.ts --store <owned-store>`, written below as `orch`. `ORCH_STORE` is the alternative explicit binding. Plain TSV and JSON stay readable without the CLI.\\n\\n- `preferences.md` is the standing-orders register: numbered lines, one constraint each (model policy, stack shape and count, verification bar, forbidden paths, escalation policy). Paste it verbatim into every spawn and every resume. Directives decay across resumes, and each dropped one costs a human turn. When you catch yourself restating an instruction, append the line before you act (principle-encode-lessons-in-structure).\\n- `overview.md` is the durable PR and issue DB. Append. Never rewrite wholesale per event.\\n- `units.tsv` has one row per unit: id, track, state, branch, PR, head SHA, brief path. Update rows in place.\\n- `frontier.json` is the computed merge frontier, per Stack safety.\\n- `ledger.tsv` is the verification ledger, per Verification.\\n- `inbox/` holds completion pointers. `gates.md` parks human gates (question, options, default on no answer).\\n- `decisions.tsv` is the trail via the show-me-your-work skill.\\n- `status.md` is derived from `units.tsv` and `ledger.tsv` at each drain, never hand-maintained. Regenerate it from the tables instead of narrating events into it.\\n\\n\\n#### Helper contract\\n\\nRead [orch CLI](../scripts/orch/orch.ts), [store](../scripts/orch/store.ts), [tests](../scripts/orch/orch.test.ts), [bootstrap](../scripts/bootstrap.ts), [manifest](../scripts/package.json) and [lock](../scripts/bun.lock). The CLI requires the exact pinned dependencies in a separately authorized writable copy. The operative package has no installed dependencies; the tested helper snapshot is evidence for that snapshot only. No automatic install occurs. Read docs/testing/helper-setup.md for the exact-copy validation boundary and retained historical setup evidence. It grants no installation approval and transfers no historical pass to this caller. Any future setup needs fresh explicit authorization for the exact writable copy, registry, disabled lifecycle scripts and task-owned cache under Herd. Missing dependencies block execution.\\n\\nUse these actual commands through the explicit `orch` binding:\\n\\n- `init`; `standing add <line>`; `standing show --json`. Compact standing output truncates after four rows, so use JSON or read preferences.md to obtain every standing order.\\n- `unit add <id> --track <track> --brief <path>`; `unit set <id> --state <state> --branch <branch> --pr <number> --sha <full-head-sha>`; `unit get <id>`; `unit list --json`.\\n- `ledger record <pr> <full-head-sha> <verdict> --evidence <path> --verifier <identity>`; `ledger check <pr> <full-head-sha>`; `ledger summary`. A missing exact key returns NOT-VERIFIED and exit 2. Usage or runtime failure returns exit 1; success returns 0.\\n- `inbox push <agent> <unit> <status> --report <path>`; `inbox drain --peek --json`; `inbox drain --json`; `inbox count`. Peek before drain, persist that receipt to an owned artifact and read it back. Capture the complete actual drain output to another owned receipt and verify readback before classifying pointers. Drain removes the queued pointers; arrivals between peek and drain can change the actual batch. If the receipt is lost or interruption makes consumption uncertain, reconcile actual artifacts before retrying or updating rows.\\n- `gate park <id> --question <question> --options <options> --default <answer>`; `gate list --json`; `gate resolve <id> --answer <answer>`. Resolve permission gates only from actual authorization.\\n- `frontier set --repo <stack-owner-clone>`, optionally `--prs <bottom-to-top-numbers>`; `frontier show --json`; `status`. Frontier discovery runs local git and gt inspection against that clone. Missing gt metadata, malformed output or pin mismatch is an error, never guessed frontier state.\\n\\nThe helper does not spawn, wait, wake, enforce worker ownership, validate full revision syntax for unit or ledger input, inspect evidence paths, enforce terminal states or verify permissions. Keep immutable assignments and append-only attempts separately under the assignment contract. Match identity, input revision, full current head SHA, artifacts and observed method before accepting results. Ledger counts include historical revisions; filter against the current unit and frontier heads before counting verified completions. A done unit string, ledger label or open-gate count proves no worker completion or authorization. Coordinator-owned bookkeeping may record worker facts; give each worker separate result and receipt paths. Atomic rename is not proof of crash durability or safe adversarial concurrent access.\\n\\n#### The brief\\n\\nYour prompts to agents are your only product, and a sloppy brief compounds into slop across the whole tree. Every spawn carries all of it. A field you cannot fill is a unit you have not scoped yet.\\n\\n```\\nGOAL         one sentence, the outcome, executable by a stranger with no chat access\\nSCOPE        paths this unit may write; paths it may not; its exclusive worktree or branch\\nCONTEXT      pointers to files and PRs; upstream reports pasted in full when this unit\\n             depends on them, because workers cannot see siblings\\nACCEPTANCE   checkable criteria, one per line\\nVERIFY       exact commands or the control-skill path, plus known gotchas\\nTIMEBOX      rough cap on runtime; on expiry, return partial findings and stop rather than run on\\nFORBIDDEN    no gt, no rebase, no force-push, no fixes outside scope, plus unit-specific bans\\nREPORT       status, branch, head SHA, PRs, verdict, what you actually ran, deviations,\\n             suggested follow-ups\\nSTANDING     <preferences.md pasted verbatim>\\n```\\n\\nSize the brief to the unit. A one-command unit gets the template collapsed to a paragraph that still names goal, scope, the verify command, and the report shape. A 4KB scaffold around a two-line edit costs more to write and obey than the edit. A verified readable local standing-orders path may supply the exact text. Paste it verbatim for remote spawns and every resume. Never replace it with a summary.\\n\\nA sub-coordinator brief adds its track boundary and unit list, its spawn budget with supported remote placement and the local exception list, the drain protocol, and the rollup format (per child: name, status, PR, head SHA, verdict, one line, plus track status and frontier delta).\\n\\nA dependency is a context relay, not just ordering. Undeclared upstream context makes the worker guess. Missing fields are a refuse-to-spawn condition. Audit one sampled worker brief per sub-coordinator per wave, concurrently with the wave it samples, never as a gate in front of it. A failing brief stops that track and fixes the sub-coordinator's instructions, not just the worker, because brief quality decays late in a run. Never resume-chain a brief. Respawn fresh with consolidated scope.\\n\\n#### Steps\\n\\n1. **Frame.** State the done predicate as something countable (\\\"all 126 units merged, each verified at each current full head SHA with `unit-test-verified` or better\\\"). Quantify scope: units, rough effort, expected stacks, and the wall-clock budget. If one agent could finish inside that budget, stop here and run Autonomous run instead. Collapsing must not depend on another document being present. It means do the work directly in this session, plain workers where they help, verification inline, landing as you go, and none of the store, register, or pilot machinery below. Schedule landing against the budget. By roughly 70% of it, stop spawning and land what is verified. Name the tracks per project. A contested decomposition or one-way door goes through the arena skill before the pilot. Present the framing once. Reversible prep proceeds without waiting.\\n2. **Initialize the runtime.** Check the helper prerequisites, then run `orch init`. Initialization creates bookkeeping files, not dependencies or workers. Open the trail via the show-me-your-work skill, write the standing orders before any spawn, and seed `frontier.json` from existing PRs with `orch frontier set --repo <repo-dir>`.\\n3. **Pilot.** Push one unit through the whole path: brief, worker, verification, stack entry, ledger row, merge. The pilot exists to falsify the brief template, the verify recipe, and the unit size while that costs one agent instead of fifty. Fix the contract from pilot evidence before any fan-out. Scale the pilot to the unit. On programs of near-identical cheap units, the first unit is the pilot, run as a normal unit with its verify command inline, and fan-out starts the moment it lands. The dedicated pilot pipeline (separate verifier agent, audit gate) is for expensive or novel unit shapes, not for clone-units where a serialized pilot has nothing to falsify.\\n4. **Scale.** Spawn a rolling window of workers up to the in-flight cap, refilling as children finish. Blocking batches pay the slowest child of every batch. Spawn track sub-coordinators only past the one-drain threshold in Roles. Recompute ready work after each drain. Relay upstream reports into downstream briefs. Keep sibling communication upward only. The sampled brief audit runs alongside the wave it samples and stops the next refill on failure, not the current one.\\n5. **Drain.** Run the queue discipline below at every drain point.\\n6. **Land.** Landing is continuous, never a terminal phase. Integration starts with the first verified unit and runs alongside the remaining waves. On heavy repos the stacker is a standing role from wave one, integrating as units verify. On repos where local git is cheap, the coordinator lands verified units itself per Roles. Keep the frontier green before upper-stack work. Stack safety governs. Advance `frontier.json` only on merge or reported new head SHAs.\\n7. **Close.** Drain the final inbox, reconcile every spawned agent to a terminal row (done, abandoned, zombie-reconciled), confirm the predicate on the real artifact, confirm every landed PR has a verdict for its current head SHA, audit the trail per show-me-your-work including its cross-model review, encode recurring corrections into `preferences.md` or the brief template. Leave the store intact. It is the postmortem.\\n\\n#### Queue and drain\\n\\n- On a completion notification, run `orch inbox push <agent> <unit> <status> [--report PATH]` and return to what you were doing. Never deep-review inline. A completion that needs review becomes a verifier unit. Never review a diff inside a drain.\\n- Drain in batches at four points: the end of a critical section, a track rollup, a frontier watcher wake (arm it through an exposed authorized wake binding, with a long heartbeat fallback when explicitly authorized), and before a human report. Begin each batch with the peek-and-receipt protocol above, then `orch inbox drain --json`. Preserve completion notifications that arrive during drain for the next batch. A concurrent helper writer can fail on the store lock; keep that pointer externally and enqueue it at the next safe boundary instead of treating it as saved.\\n- Critical sections you finish first: authoring a brief, a stack operation, a conflict decision, writing a gate, updating ledger or frontier.\\n- Each drain classifies every pointer (landed, needs-verify, failed, zombie, noise), writes the resulting rows through `orch unit add`, `orch unit set`, and `orch ledger record`, runs `orch status`, then spawns the next wave in one message.\\n- Account for every spawned child at its track's rollup: arrived, respawned, or its scope explicitly absorbed. Silently redoing a missing child's work hides both the wasted spend and the coverage gap its result existed to close.\\n- A drain turn ends with the three lines from `orch status`: counts against the states, what changed, gates open. Detail lives in `status.md`. The full reply contract applies at checkpoints and close.\\n\\n#### Stack safety\\n\\n- The frontier is a computed object, never narrative. Recompute `frontier.json` from `gt` after every merge and stack mutation because GitHub base refs drift mid-restack while gt tracking is authoritative: ordered PR list, branch names, head SHAs, a generation number, the lowest unmerged PR. Resolve it where gt knows the stack, normally the stacker's clone. A checkout whose gt metadata never saw the submits reports no PRs and the command errors rather than guessing.\\n- Exactly one stacker per stack may run `gt`, serialized within its stack. Record the holder in the standing orders. Prefer remote restacks when supported and authorized. Missing remote placement remains a limit; never silently substitute local heavy work.\\n- Workers never rebase and never run `gt`. Babysitters follow `playbooks/babysit.md`, one per stack, scoped to one immutable frontier generation. They report conflicts to the stacker rather than restacking.\\n- PR closes and retargets go through the stacker only. Closing a base PR orphans every chain above it. Merges and stack surgery are units with briefs like any other.\\n- One retro watcher follows merged PRs for reverts, post-merge CI breaks, and orphaned follow-ups.\\n\\n#### Verification\\n\\nScale verification to the unit. When VERIFY is a single cheap command, the worker runs it and reports the output, and the coordinator spot-checks receipts. A dedicated verifier agent (on a different model family than the worker) is for units whose verification is expensive, judgment-laden, or high-blast-radius. A verifier agent whose entire product would be rerunning one command is ceremony, not verification.\\n\\nWrite ledger rows with `orch ledger record`. Check the current PR and head SHA with `orch ledger check`. `ledger.tsv`, one row per verdict, keyed by PR number plus head SHA: `live-ui-verified | unit-test-verified | type-check-only | verifier-blocked | verifier-failed`. CI green is an input to a verdict, not a verdict. Behavioral work needs better than `type-check-only`. `verifier-blocked` is not a pass. Respawn when the environment heals. `verifier-failed` gets a fix unit, not a re-verify. A worker may self-report. The coordinator inspects the method evidence and lets a verifier override it on the same key. The helper replaces a row on that key regardless of role; callers must enforce precedence and preserve attempt history separately. A new head SHA voids the row, so re-verify after restack. The ledger answers \\\"was this verified\\\", not memory and not the transcript.\\n\\nA unit is not done until its output is externalized the moment it lands, never batched to the end of the run. An authorized worker pushes its branch, the designated ledger owner records the inspected verifier result, and receipts land in the store. Without push permission, externalization is limited to the authorized durable artifact and landing remains pending. Work that exists only on one VM when that VM dies was never done.\\n\\n#### Liveness and failure\\n\\n- Never resume an agent to check on it. A follow-up can restart an idle worker; inspect its actual state before use. Probe read-only: the ledger, `units.tsv`, `gh`, pushed branches, the worker's observed status through the exposed inspection binding. Transcript mtime is not liveness.\\n- A silent death gets a synthetic postmortem row in the inbox (unit, failure mode, last evidence, options). Replan on evidence as it arrives. Never wait for full quiescence.\\n- Retry by mode: cap-hit or oom, respawn with smaller scope. Network-drop, retry as-is. Tool-error, retry on a different model. Unknown, retry once. Two retries, then abandon the unit and replan around it. Missing required SHA or method evidence uses the stricter assignment limit of one inspected retry. A changed scope or input revision gets a new assignment ID linked to its predecessor. Never retry denied permissions or unknown external outcomes into success.\\n- A zombie that returns hours late reconciles against the current frontier and ledger before anything is accepted. Salvage unique findings through a fresh unit, never a blind merge.\\n- When continued spawning would produce garbage tree-wide (bad upstream output, broken acceptance, dead infra), write a stop line at the top of the standing orders, let in-flight work finish, fix the cause, clear it.\\n- Bound your own infra retries the same way you bound a child's. After a few consecutive tool aborts, stop retrying. Write a terminal handoff to durable state (what is done, where it lives, the exact command to resume) and end the run.\\n- After a host restart, inspect worker state. Do not infer that local agents died or remote work survived. Re-read the standing orders and `units.tsv`, recompute the frontier, reattach surviving remote work by inspected PR and branch plus immutable assignment identity rather than stale agent id, respawn one sub-coordinator per track from its stored brief plus current state, drain, resume. A dead holder does not authorize takeover. `orch` rejects a stale lock until ownership review. Copy and fill [`feature-map.example.md`](./feature-map.example.md) outside `automations/benny/` instead of editing the copied example.\\n\\nIf the skill, feature map, or a required capability is absent, ambiguous, or incomplete, repro and fix work must fail closed.\\n\\n## Required capabilities\\n\\n### Bring up\\n\\nStart the requested app revision in the requested test environment.\\n\\nInput:\\n\\n- Repository and revision\\n- Build or start mode\\n- Workspace, account, fixture, and feature-state requirements\\n- Artifact directory\\n- Completed feature-map path\\n\\nReturn:\\n\\n- Session identifier\\n- How the adapter confirmed the correct app and environment\\n- Stable app markers\\n- Running process or target details needed by later calls\\n- Any missing capability\\n\\nThe adapter must distinguish the target app from a similar window, shell, or production instance.\\n\\n### Drive UI\\n\\nPerform real user actions:\\n\\n- Click\\n- Type\\n- Press keys\\n- Scroll\\n- Drag\\n- Resize\\n- Navigate through app controls\\n\\nPrefer roles, labels, and stable selectors. Use coordinates only after a fresh screenshot.\\n\\nReturn each action and the observed state change.\\n\\nDo not set internal state, call hidden app methods, write directly to storage, or inject DOM changes to create the symptom.\\n\\n### Drive mapped features and states\\n\\nRead the relevant feature-map section before driving the app.\\n\\nThe adapter must expose ways to:\\n\\n- Navigate every mapped feature through the user-visible path.\\n- Invoke the adapter action names listed for that feature.\\n- Interact with default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, loading, empty, error, selected, open, expanded, and feature-specific states when they apply.\\n- Arrange a state through safe fixture data, permissions, flags, service responses, or supported test controls.\\n- Reset the feature for a second independent repro attempt.\\n- Capture the screenshot, video, and read-only cross-check named by the feature map.\\n\\nUse roles, accessible names, ARIA relationships, stable component markers, and purpose-named data attributes. Never use generated CSS or StyleX classes, dynamic hashes, child indexes, or brittle DOM position.\\n\\nArranging a precondition is not permission to inject the reported symptom. The repro itself must still come from real user interaction.\\n\\n### Inspect state\\n\\nRead state to confirm what the UI shows.\\n\\nExamples:\\n\\n- Accessibility tree\\n- DOM or view hierarchy\\n- Process state\\n- Local logs\\n- Network request status\\n- App-exposed debug state\\n\\nInspection is read-only. If a query changes state, it belongs in `drive UI` and must represent a real user action.\\n\\n### Screenshot\\n\\nCapture the current app state to a requested path.\\n\\nReturn:\\n\\n- File path\\n- Capture time\\n- App marker or window title\\n- Short description of what should be visible\\n\\nThe screenshot must show enough app chrome to prove that the correct app is under test.\\n\\n### Recording\\n\\nStart and stop a screen recording around the full repro path.\\n\\nReturn:\\n\\n- File path\\n- Start and stop times\\n- Captured window or region\\n- Whether audio or sensitive overlays were omitted\\n\\nThe recording must show the discriminating final state, not only setup or a loading screen.\\n\\n### Cleanup\\n\\nStop processes and sessions created by the adapter.\\n\\nRemove disposable:\\n\\n- Browser or app profiles\\n- Temporary workspaces\\n- Test accounts or fixtures when the adapter created them\\n- Debug ports and tunnels\\n- Captures past their retention window\\n\\nReturn what was stopped, removed, retained, or left for a person.\\n\\nCleanup must not delete user work.\\n\\n## Adapter behavior\\n\\nThe adapter must:\\n\\n- Report capabilities before the repro starts.\\n- Report which feature-map sections it can drive and which are blocked.\\n- Use the same environment inputs for baseline and patched builds.\\n- Surface startup failures as failures.\\n- Bound retries.\\n- Keep secrets out of logs and artifacts.\\n- Keep captures outside the repository.\\n- Support a fresh or reset state between the two repro attempts.\\n- Avoid production changes unless the user explicitly configured a safe test action.\\n\\n## Environment translation\\n\\nBefore declaring an environment block, restate the defect without platform-specific nouns and ask whether the same behavior can be tested safely in the available environment.\\n\\nExamples:\\n\\n- A named browser may mean any external browser.\\n- A named key may mean the configured shortcut.\\n- A named remote host may mean a delayed or disconnected remote target.\\n\\nUse a translated attempt only when it tests the same underlying behavior. Label it as translated evidence. Do not call it an exact repro when the missing environment is part of the defect.\\n\\nHardware prompts, operating-system permission dialogs, device-only APIs, and unavailable account states may be real blocks.\\n\\n## Setup check\\n\\nBefore enabling the repro automation, first review supplied or inert evidence for this adapter check. Actually starting apps, driving disposable states, capturing media, or cleaning fixtures requires separately authorized test scope. With that scope, run one harmless adapter check:\\n\\n1. Bring up the app.\\n2. Confirm the stable app marker.\\n3. Load one completed feature-map section.\\n4. Navigate to that feature through its user path.\\n5. Exercise one disposable state through mapped adapter actions.\\n6. Inspect the resulting state.\\n7. Capture a screenshot.\\n8. Record a short clip.\\n9. Clean up.\\n\\nEnable repro work only when all nine steps succeed and no source-channel Slack post is involved.\\n\\nMissing or denied capabilities block repro. Fixture review is structural only and cannot satisfy the nine live adapter steps.\\n\\nSOURCE automations/benny/skills/reproduce-and-fix-issues/references/verify-existing-fix.md\\n# Verify an existing fix\\n\\nUse this mode when an open pull request or merged commit plausibly fixes the report.\\n\\nThe existing artifact owns the fix. Verify it. Do not edit it, author a competing patch, or open another pull request.\\n\\n## Qualify the artifact\\n\\nRequire one concrete artifact:\\n\\n- An open pull request with code changes that address the symptom\\n- A merged pull request\\n- A merged commit with matching code and intent\\n\\nA thread claim, tracker status, branch name, or cause hypothesis without a pull request or commit is not enough.\\n\\nWhen several artifacts exist, choose the one linked from the source thread or tracker. Otherwise choose the closest match to the affected code and state why.\\n\\n## Protect the working tree\\n\\nUse an isolated worktree or another clean checkout when the repository supports it. Do not overwrite user changes.\\n\\nRecord:\\n\\n- Baseline revision\\n- Patched revision\\n- Pull request or commit URL\\n- Build and environment inputs shared by both runs\\n\\nUse regular `github.com` pull request links.\\n\\n## Measure the baseline\\n\\nFor an open pull request, use its base branch as the baseline.\\n\\nFor a merged fix, use the revision immediately before the fix when that revision builds and represents the old behavior.\\n\\nThrough the configured control adapter:\\n\\n1. Bring up the baseline app.\\n2. Confirm the correct app and environment.\\n3. Run the reported path through real UI actions.\\n4. Observe the discriminating symptom.\\n5. Reset and repeat it.\\n6. Capture baseline recording, screenshot, and state check.\\n\\nIf the symptom does not appear twice on the baseline, there is no baseline. Do not claim that the fix works.\\n\\n## Measure the patched build\\n\\nBuild and run the pull request or fix commit with the same environment and data.\\n\\n1. Run the same UI path.\\n2. Repeat it twice.\\n3. Confirm that the broken state is gone.\\n4. Confirm the expected state appears.\\n5. Capture after recording, screenshot, and the same state check.\\n\\nDo not stop at compilation or tests. The after result must come from a running patched app.\\n\\n## Outcomes\\n\\n### Confirmed\\n\\nThe baseline reproduces twice and the patched build resolves it twice.\\n\\n- Mark operations status as verified.\\n- Link the artifact.\\n- Post one concise source-thread reply after the source preflight.\\n- Include the before and after result.\\n- Open no pull request.\\n\\n### Insufficient fix\\n\\nThe symptom appears on both baseline and patched builds.\\n\\n- Mark operations status as reproduced but not fixed.\\n- Link the artifact and say it did not resolve the symptom.\\n- Post the normal confirmed-repro source update if the run has not already used it.\\n- Open no competing pull request.\\n\\n### Inconclusive\\n\\nThe baseline does not reproduce, the patched app cannot run, or the evidence does not show the discriminating state.\\n\\n- Do not claim success.\\n- State which half could not be measured.\\n- Keep the result in the operations thread or run output.\\n- Post nothing in the source thread unless a direct question requires an answer.\\n\\n## Cleanup\\n\\nStop both builds, remove temporary profiles and captures according to retention policy, and return the repository to its prior state without discarding user work.\\n\\nRepository checkout changes and adapter execution require authorized isolated test scope. Message and status writes need separate destination authorization. If unavailable, retain the verification plan locally and report blocked.
